- **`ios-app/scripts/heredoc_backtick_check.sh` — the meta-gate now walks `ios-app/scripts/` recursively.** Its stated goal was "no shell script in this tree splices a backtick into an interpolating heredoc", but its file list came from `"$SCRIPTS"/*.sh`, which cannot see a subdirectory. That was harmless while every harness was a top-level file; the widget-surface checks now live one file per surface under `scripts/widget_view_dispatch/`, so a subject could leave the audited population simply by moving down one directory — the same "the guard cannot see it" defect the gate exists to close, expressed as a path instead of as a line number. The population now comes from `find "$SCRIPTS" ! -type d -name '*.sh' -print0 | LC_ALL=C sort -z`: sorted so two runs diff cleanly, `! -type d` rather than `-type f` because the glob it replaces matched symlinks and a symlinked `.sh` is as executable as a real one, and an entry that is not readable is refused instead of contributing zero records. Every rule (R1/R2/R3), the vacuity guard and the summary line are unchanged; a finding names its file by path relative to `scripts/` so two same-named files in different directories cannot be confused. The "subdirs are NOT scanned" disclaimer is replaced by measured `cover`/`limit` lines describing what the recursive walk actually saw on this run.
- **`ios-app/scripts/heredoc_backtick_check.sh` — the per-file `bytes=N` column was 4x the number of lines carrying the byte, and is now `lines-with-byte=N`, counted from the records that actually drive the verdicts.** `N` came from `nwords "$hits"`, and `hits` was built by printing the whole HIT record per matching line — `HIT<TAB>region<TAB>line<TAB>expanding`, four tab-separated fields — so the word count reported four words per line: `build_check.sh` carries the byte on 3 lines and printed 12, `sf_symbol_check.sh` on 8 and printed 32, in every file and in both directions of the recursion change, with rc=0 and a clean summary. Nothing else could see it: the findings count records, the `measured-inert` total counts a list that is one word per record, and a constant factor leaves both green. The column is exactly what the gate's own header promises a reader can check ("all of them are measured on the tree being scanned, on this run"), so a reader who grepped for the byte got a number that was neither a byte count nor a line count. The value is now the number of HIT **records** — the verdict machinery is per line, so a line count is the number the rules use; the gate's only byte count remains the `tr`-measured one it prints for a skipped `.golden`. The two columns on the same line that read as counts and never were one now say what they hold: `unquoted-openers-at=` (line:delimiter pairs) and `quoted-openers-at=` (line numbers), where `quoted-heredoc=29` previously read like a count of 29 and named one line. `here-strings=` and `operator-mentions=` are counts and keep their names. Verdicts, enumeration and the `summary:` line are unchanged (measured on this tree: 45 scanned / 0 findings / 169 measured-inert / rc=0).

Real hermes is evicted from `sys.modules` explicitly rather than via `monkeypatch.delitem`, which restores only keys that existed and would otherwise hand the next case in the process a fake `hermes_cli` whose tmp dir is still on disk.

- **Two guards, each covering what the other cannot.** A static ban runs as the
  gate's FIRST executable code and refuses the file before a heredoc is ever
  expanded, naming the offending line numbers. It fails closed: grep rc 0 means
  "the byte was found" and rc ≥ 2 means "the guard could not read the file it is
  judging" — both refuse, because a guard that waves a run through after failing
  to look is not a guard. It judges `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}`, the file actually
  executing, not a hardcoded leaf name: a mutated renamed copy sitting beside a
  clean canonical gate is now refused, where the leaf-name version audited the
  clean neighbour and let the copy through. At the foot of the gate, before the
  harness binary is run, the generated `$WORK/main.swift` must be **byte-identical
  to the committed `ios-app/scripts/widget_settings_check.harness.golden`**. That
  half is a drift check and is described as one: the harness is assembled from
  `$model`, `$suite` and `$wkey` lifted out of `Sources/` at run time, so anything
  that moves in those inputs moves these bytes, and a harness whose bytes moved is
  a harness whose assertions moved. It is **not** a backtick detector and no longer
  claims to be — the harness legitimately carries backticks (the extracted model's
  own doc comments use them), and a backtick arriving through an expansion is
  inert text either way.
- **`widget_settings_check_backtick_probe.sh` is that proof, kept in-tree.** A
  guard whose only evidence is a claim in a comment is a guard nobody has seen
  fire, and "the gate exits 0" proves nothing about a defect that exits 0 while
  executing shell. The probe plants a marker-writing payload into every context the
  gate can expand — each unquoted heredoc region (openers enumerated at run time,
  so a second heredoc is covered without editing the probe: hardcoding one opener
  is what let the first payload through), shell position above and below the
  heredoc, a renamed copy with the canonical gate clean beside it, and a real `#`
  comment — and requires per leg that no marker file appears AND that the guard
  refused, rather than the payload having been inert by luck. It also runs an
  unmodified copy and requires it still to pass, so a guard that refuses everything
  cannot score green here, and it verifies it never mutated the gate. Before the
  fix: 5 legs red, payloads executed. After: every planted leg refused before
  execution, control green, gate sha unchanged. It carries no backtick of its own
  (`printf '\140'`), because a probe holding the banned byte is disqualified by the
  rule it tests.
- **Its one honest limit, printed every run — and made smaller.** A guard can
  only judge the text at or below its own first executable statement. The first
  version of this fix left that statement sitting below its own documentation and
  measured the span from the guard's comment paragraph: the probe reported an
  uncovered prologue of 4 lines when the ban statement was 48 lines down, so 46
  insertable lines were in fact unjudged, and a payload planted one line below
  the anchor the probe called the boundary executed. Two changes. The probe now
  anchors on a `GUARD-FIRST-EXEC` marker on the ban statement itself (deriving it
  as the first non-comment line after the sentinel if the marker is lost) and
  refuses to print a figure at all when the anchor lands on a comment line or
  above the sentinel — a boundary that is guessed is the bug the leg exists to
  catch. And the ban moved above its own prose, so the span it cannot judge is now
  the shebang, the `set` line and a three-line pointer. The figure is the probe's
  to print, not this file's to remember. Reported, never passed: whoever can write
  above the guard can also delete it, and closing that for real needs a meta-gate
  scanning every script in `ios-app/scripts/`, which is its own task
  (`t_4558fd32`) rather than a longer comment here.
- **Measured, not asserted.** Against `origin/main` @ `3b5e475c` the gate emitted
  the 3 stderr lines and generated a harness missing those 6 backticks; with the
  fix, the diff of the two generated harnesses is exactly the 3 restored comment
  lines and nothing else — the assertions are untouched. A clean run prints `99`
  `ok:` assertions, `0` `FAIL:`, the three banners (`WIDGET SETTINGS CHECK
  PASSED …`, `INTENT DELEGATION CHECK PASSED …`, `CONFIG SCREEN CHECK PASSED …`)
  and **zero bytes of stderr**, RC 0, from `ios-app/` and from the repo root. The
  golden-mismatch negative is proven too: tampering one line of the golden gives
  RC 1 with **no** assertion and **no** banner on stdout — which is why the
  integrity checks sit between the compile and the run, and why the probe demands
  zero banners on a refused leg. That check earned its keep during this change: it
  caught the fix's own first attempt (`$BT defaults` rendering one extra space)
  before a single assertion ran. `build_check.sh`, `check_sources.sh`,
  `check_theme.sh` and `python3 scripts/changelog_fragments.py check` all RC 0;
  `project.yml` is untouched (no source file added) and both new files live in
  `scripts/`, outside every target.
- **Why the escape-parity counter was dropped rather than fixed.** The first
  version counted *unescaped* backticks, which needed a backslash-parity loop,
  which hit a macOS trap worth recording: BSD awk treats a `$` in the MIDDLE of a
  regex as a literal dollar sign, so `match(head, /\$/)` never fails on ordinary
  text and such a loop spins instead of terminating. The counter is gone now — a
  whole-file ban has nothing to count — but the trap is real for anyone writing awk
  on this host.

- **`ios-app/scripts/heredoc_backtick_check_probe.sh` — the probe now agrees with the gate about what "every script" means, and proves the widened scan can actually fail.** A probe that globbed one directory would have kept agreeing with a gate that had silently lost a subtree, which is the opposite of a cross-check, so its own enumeration became the same recursive walk (`all_sh`), its digest now covers the whole population, and its private trees build real subdirectories instead of symlinking a directory — `find` does not descend a symlink it was not told to follow, so a symlinked subtree would have made every leg report green on files it never entered. Two new leg groups, each with the liveness half this class requires: `scope` compares the gate's per-file population against the probe's own enumeration **path for path** (a count would not catch the failure this card is about) and asserts the limits block no longer disclaims directories the walk enters; `depth-live`/`depth-scan` plant an unquoted heredoc carrying the byte in a script below `scripts/`, first EXECUTE it so the position is proven live there, then require the scan to refuse and name it by path. Plus `link-edge` and `samename`, the two silent-green shapes the new enumeration could otherwise create: a dangling symlink (zero records) must refuse rather than read as clean, a symlink to a real script must still be in the population, and two `common.sh` files in different directories must be told apart by path — every other leg already runs against a `scripts/` tree made entirely of symlinks, so a `-type f` regression reddens the whole probe by itself. Measured on one tree (`main` @ `c66aa7c6` plus these commits): the pre-change gate reports 39 scanned / 148 measured-inert / rc=0 while printing that the six `widget_view_dispatch/*.sh` files are not scanned, and the widened gate reports 45 scanned / 169 measured-inert / rc=0 with those six listed as covered; the same planted splice is invisible to the pre-change gate (rc=0, 0 of 6 subtree files in its population) and refused by the widened one (rc=1, 12 findings, `widget_view_dispatch/common.sh:221`). The probe is green on that tree with `scope` reporting 45 scripts path for path, 6 of them below `scripts/`.
- **`ios-app/scripts/heredoc_backtick_check_probe.sh` — a `measure` leg checks every printed per-file count against a measurement taken outside the record machinery, so a mislabelled count can no longer sit green.** Every other leg reads the gate's records or its summary, which is precisely why a 4x factor in a printed column survived: the new leg compares `lines-with-byte=` against `grep -c` for **every** scanned file (45 on this tree) and prints, for a file with none, one and many matching lines, the three numbers side by side — `check_theme.sh` prints 1, `grep -c` says 1 line, `tr` says 2 bytes; `board_status_widget_check.sh` prints 24, `grep -c` says 24, `tr` says 66 — so the equality is in the run output instead of asserted in prose, and the label's meaning is checked rather than trusted. `cmp` proves each compared file is byte-identical between the real tree and the private mirror the gate scanned, so the pair is one file measured two ways. Two negatives, both planted in private copy trees and never in the real tree: restoring the old word count reddens the leg for 29 files (rc=1) with no other leg disturbed, and renaming the label away makes all 45 report a missing column (rc=1) rather than passing on nothing. The `scope` leg's population parse keyed on the old `bytes=` label and is now label-independent (the path is the second field of a `scanned` line), so a future rename can neither redden it nor — the worse failure — make it compare nothing; the measure leg is deliberately the opposite, bound to the label because the label is what it audits. Measured on this tree: probe rc=0 with 94 ok / 0 FAIL (was 89 ok; no leg removed), and `probes_check.sh` runs it in CI by glob.
- **`ios-app/scripts/live_activity_rehydration_check.sh` — the projection joins
  the executed table: 124 → 154 rows.** A third `GATE-SLICE` block
  (`cluster-health-projection-rules`) is sliced out of
  `Sources/Shared/ClusterHealthActivity.swift` by the same awk rule and compiled
  with the harness, alongside the real `ClusterNodeTally` — so the table runs the
  code the driver pushes through, not a transcription of it. 30 new assertions
  cover: the state-word map and the one route to `unreachable` (a live read can
  never print it); `up`/`waking`/`down`/unmodelled/absent-state; a degraded
  `{speak}` body and an empty host list both yielding **no counts** while a
  stated `0 down` stays a fact; 4 listed / 2 errored yielding `2 up`, `2 down`,
  total `4` and `.3`/`.4` named in listed order, with no input address ever
  reaching a label (§7); the state read's failure label beating the node read's
  (it is the headline); a failed node read nils its counts and the headline
  becomes the gap — **`— up`, never `0/4 up`**; and the two cases the sweep must
  NOT end (a blind push, and a tally the operator switched off). The new marker
  was proven to bite by renaming it (rc 1, `FAIL: … has no
  'GATE-SLICE-BEGIN: cluster-health-projection-rules' marker`) and restoring it.
  `cluster_widget_check.sh` compiles the tally too — the widget's side of the
  same code, 78 assertions, still green.
- **`ios-app/scripts/live_activity_rehydration_check.sh` — extended to the
  running-cards activity, by slicing rather than transcribing.** 25 new
  assertions over the orphan rule (rows + fresh push keep; rows past the
  silence budget end; **zero rows end at any age**, including a fresh one and
  one stamped in the future — an empty bubble is never "still in flight") and
  over the reading rules (server count beats the rows; a subset with no count
  yields `nil`; a blind headline contains no zero; `99+` clipping; `— blocked`
  distinct from `0 blocked`; a clock ahead of the device reads `now`).
  `live_activity_rehydration_check/main.swift` copies none of it: the script
  extracts the two `GATE-SLICE` blocks out of `CardsRunningActivity.swift` and
  compiles them with the harness, so the table runs against the code the app
  and the extension actually build, and a moved marker fails the script **by
  name** instead of quietly shrinking the table. Proven red on purpose by
  renaming one marker (`FAIL: … has no 'GATE-SLICE-BEGIN:
  cards-orphan-decision' marker`, rc 1) and restoring it.
- **`ios-app/scripts/widget_view_dispatch_check.sh`, `widget_settings_check.sh` and `sf_symbol_check.sh` — the gates that now cover this behaviour, and the negative tests run against them.** `widget_view_dispatch_check.sh` gained a `widget_surface_gate` function and one call per widget this card touched: the bodies are grepped for the one-step gate (6 for the monitor panel, 5 for running cards, where the sixth family is the entry's `inlineLine`), the paused copy is asserted to have exactly one CODE owner per file, the paused-before-client order is measured INSIDE the function that owns it (a file-global line comparison reads a `makeIfConfigured()` elsewhere in the same file and fails for the wrong reason), and each cadence function is sliced out of the committed source by an END-ANCHORED `GATE-SLICE` marker and executed — Off and a corrupt negative both mean "no next date", 5/60 min are exactly +300s/+3600s. The board tile's hand-written section from #340 is left exactly as it shipped; converting it to a call here would rewrite a merged card's gate for no added coverage. `widget_settings_check.sh` pins both raw values to their literals and adds an executed block per surface: absent entry means ON (absent is never paused), the first-launch seed from `AppGroupWidgetSettings.defaults()` must also be ON at the 5-minute widget cadence (that function derives from `isLiveActivity`, so a wrong branch there is every device refreshing three times too slowly, quietly), and a surface declaring no sections must end up with NONE even when a foreign blob claims `["state"]`. `sf_symbol_check.sh` now extracts `displayIcon`'s switch body and both arms of a `systemName:` ternary, which is how `pause.circle` — drawn only inside a ternary, in both widgets — reaches a gate at all.

  Three negatives were run against the new gate, each observed to fail by name and then restored byte-for-byte (sha256 of the subject file compared before and after): suffixing either `GATE-SLICE` marker ("GATE-SLICE marker cards_running_cadence missing from …"), un-gating the bodies ("only 0 bodies gate on !configured||paused (want >= 5)"), and adding a second non-comment owner of the paused copy ("…appears 2 times (want exactly 1)"). The third one fired for real on the first attempt — this card's own header bullet quoting the copy made the count 2, which is why that assertion counts code lines only. And one assertion this card wrote did not survive being executed: it named `WidgetSurfaceKind.defaultSettings`, a symbol that does not exist, and the executed gate failed to compile it where a grepped gate would have waved it through forever. That is the argument for slicing and running rather than matching, in one line.

  Gate, all rc=0 and no device or simulator: `build_check` — "HSCC: 62 files, 0 error(s), 0 warning(s) / HSCCWidgets: 16 files, 0 error(s), 0 warning(s) / HSCCLiveActivity: 5 files / HSCCLiveActivityMonitor: 11 files / full compile clean, 0 warnings (compile only — never built or run on a device)"; `check_sources` — "sources in sync: 78 Swift files, all listed in project.yml"; `check_theme` — "CLEAN — no raw colour outside Theme.swift."; `actool_icon_check` — "ACTOOL ICON CHECK PASSED — AppIcon compiles and is wired (still not verified on a device)."; `model_decode_check` — "ALL DECODE CHECKS PASSED — 87/87 checks (over 54 committed fixtures) decoded against the real models"; `shared_store_check`, `widget_settings_check`, `widget_view_dispatch_check` and `sf_symbol_check` ("PASS: all 63 SF Symbols resolve") all PASSED; `scripts/changelog_fragments.py check` — "OK — [Unreleased] is pointer". `main` moved under this card while it was in flight (#333 merged as #340, the board-status tile), so the branch is rebased onto `3b5e475c` and its `ConfigView` / `SharedStore` / `widget_settings_check.sh` hunks are resolved against that content rather than stacked on the old PR — which is also why the two new row glyphs had to be chosen to differ from the board tile's. No file was added under `Sources/`, so `project.yml` and `scripts/generate.sh` are untouched. Compile-only: nothing here was built or run on a device, so the paused pane's rendered pixels remain the on-device checklist's job.

- **`hscc-api/docs/audit-client-server-params.md` — the human-facing mirror of the two contract matrices still listed retired client routes as live, and every surviving row cited a handler line that had drifted.** `t_f09436f1` (PR #351) pruned the four dead rows from `REQUIRED_QUERY_PARAMS` / `REQUIRED_BODY_PARAMS` and added `test_matrices_name_routes_the_client_still_calls`; this card ships the half that stayed: the audit doc still had `GET /v1/memory`, `POST /v1/template/apply` and both `POST /v1/memory/{node}/*` rows in its live matrices, and both the doc and the surviving rows of the test's own audit table pointed at pre-drift lines (`routes_actions.py:199`/`:303` vs `:230`/`:334`, `routes_sessions.py:252-254`/`:291-293` vs `:254`/`:293`, `routes_orchestrator.py:1304-1310` vs `_validate_prompt` at `:1970-1975`). The doc now separates **live client contract** from **server requirement whose client call site retired**, naming the still-enforced server site on every retired row (`routes_memory.py:288`/`:315`/`:342`/`:346`, `routes_actions.py:312`) so a pruned row can never be misread as a pruned requirement; the test's kept rows gained handler names beside their lines, so the next drift leaves the citation readable. Comment- and doc-only — no assertion, matrix row or gate is touched.

## [2.15.11] - 2026-11-14

### Added
- **`orch-sync` and `reasoning-sync` now take `--hermes-home DIR`, like the
  three commands `t_d39c720e` covered.** Both resolved `rolelib.PROFILES_DIR`
  and wrote into it — `orch_sync.sync_all` rewrites `SOUL.md` (plus a
  `SOUL.md.bak-<stamp>`) and copies skill dirs into every live `<project>-orch`
  profile, `reasoning_sync.sync_all` rewrites the `agent`/`delegation`
  `reasoning_effort` keys of every profile `config.yaml` — with no intent check
  at all. They now share the single parse+apply helper `_take_home_flag`: apply
  the home, then `rolelib.assert_profile_root(<DIR>/profiles, purpose="<cmd>
  --hermes-home")` before the first write, refusal = exit **2** with stdout left
  empty (stdout on both is machine-captured JSON, so a refused run must not
  print a partial report). No flag still means no apply and no assert: what a
  real `hscc template apply` targets is unchanged.
- **`hscc-api` now asserts which profiles root it may write, and
  `HSCC_API_PROFILES_ROOT` is the only way to name one.** The env var holds the
  PROFILES DIR (`<hermes-home>/profiles`, the directory that directly contains
  `<profile>/config.yaml`) — the same contract as
  `rolelib.assert_profile_root(expected)` from PR #301, so a CLI refusal and an
  API refusal are configured and worded alike. It is read ONCE in
  `create_server()` and carried on `ApiContext.profile_root_intent`; handlers
  never re-read the environment, because a long-lived multithreaded server that
  re-resolved intent per request would be reading a value that can change
  underneath a running turn. There is deliberately no flag for it — not on an
  HTTP route, not on `serve`'s argv, not on `hscc api start` — because `serve`'s
  argv is baked into a generated launchd unit and a flag there would be a second,
  less visible channel for the same statement. Unset, empty or whitespace means
  today's behaviour, unchanged, so a `VAR=` in a plist cannot brick the server;
  the generated unit gains neither this var nor `HERMES_HOME` (a hand-added key is
  honoured). Guarding a resolver instead was ruled out as unimplementable:
  `HERMES_HOME=<root>/profiles/<name>` resolving back to the native home is *the
  mechanism hermes profile mode runs on*, so the same bytes mean "throwaway
  sandbox" and "this hermes runs under a profile" and only the caller knows which
  — which is why the knowledge has to arrive from outside the process.
- **`hscc-roles` now asserts which hermes home it is about to write, and
  `--hermes-home DIR` is the supported way to name one.** The three
  profile-writing commands (`generate`, `orch`, `orch-all`) take the flag,
  point the process at the requested root, then ask hermes' own resolver where
  the write will actually land and refuse — exit 2, stdout empty, nothing
  written — unless the answer is exactly `<DIR>/profiles`. The guard is
  `rolelib.assert_profile_root(expected)`, which resolves the roots the same way
  the writers do and checks BOTH of them: hermes' `get_profile_dir` (what
  `generate_profile` writes config.yaml/SOUL.md through) and
  `rolelib.PROFILES_DIR` (what the fallback writer and orchestrator skill
  seeding use). A plain bootstrap passes no flag, so nothing is applied and
  nothing is asserted: what an operator bootstrap targets is unchanged.

### Changed
- **`hscc cards monitor` shows whole text by default; `a` toggles the short
  preview.** Since 2.15.10 every thought was cut at 320 chars with a `…+N more`
  marker, tool arguments at 110 and user turns at 120, and only the cut line was
  stored, so no key could bring the text back. Each stored transcript entry now
  keeps both the whole and the short line (both built once when the row is
  read); the default view prints the whole one, `a` switches all/short live for
  text already on screen, and the new `--short` flag starts in the old preview
  mode for `--live` and the one-shot snapshot. The panel title clip, `READY_ROWS`
  / `+N more waiting`, `MAX_LINES`, the tools-only view and the whitespace
  collapse of a thought are unchanged. `wrap_tail` already walks from the last
  line backwards and stops once the panel height is filled, so no per-tick wrap
  of the stored buffer was added.

### Fixed
- **`hscc bootstrap` deleted every profile-config key it did not own.**
  `generate_profile()` built `config.yaml` as a dict from scratch and wrote
  that dict, so any key outside its own set vanished — the per-block
  "operator values survive" merges (`_compression_block`, `_memory_block`,
  `_merge_toolsets`, `_onboarding_block`) only ever protected the blocks the
  generator already knew about. Measured against the operator snapshot
  `pre-2.15.10-bootstrap-20261113-1328` (49 profiles): `_config_version`
  disappeared from 45 of them and the whole `browser:` section (not a nested
  leaf — the top-level key) from 25. Losing `_config_version` is not cosmetic:
  Hermes then runs its silent config migration on that profile's next start,
  so 45 profiles took an unreviewed migration none of them asked for.
  `generate_profile()` now merges its generated blocks over the file's
  COMPLETE existing mapping (existing wins key order and every key the
  generator does not emit; the generator wins only the values it computes) and
  writes through Hermes' own `atomic_config_write()`, which keeps comments,
  key order and quoting and refuses a write that would drop a mapping path —
  so this class of loss fails loudly instead of deleting operator state.
- **A "sandboxed" `orch-sync` could no longer copy the operator's real skill
  tree into a throwaway profile.** `--skills-source` defaulted to
  `<hermes-home>/skills`, but the default was computed *before* the options were
  parsed — so it always resolved to the ambient `~/.hermes/skills` even when a
  different home was requested, and a run that believed it was sandboxed read
  the operator's skill tree. The read root now follows the write root:
  `--hermes-home DIR` makes the default `DIR/skills`, and a missing pack there
  is reported under `skills_missing_source` rather than silently borrowed. An
  explicit `--skills-source` still wins, and the one root the flag deliberately
  does **not** move — the reasoning policy, read from `$HSCC_REASONING_POLICY`
  (`~/.hscc/state/reasoning_policy.json`, cluster-global config outside the
  hermes home) — is now stated in the help, the command docstrings and the
  README instead of being something a caller had to know.
- **Generated orchestrator text claimed the merge unconditionally.** Rule 5 of
  the "How you manage work" block every `<project>-orch` SOUL is built from
  read "**You review and merge your board's PRs.**". That is true only where no
  card says otherwise: on a finish rail where the worker merges its own PR into
  the integration branch once its gate is green and review happens once, on the
  branch, the sentence tells the orchestrator to redo work the worker already
  did — duplicated review, a second merge attempt, or a wait for a merge that
  never arrives. Rule 5 now separates review from merging, names the card body's
  `HANDOFF` section as the authority for who merges, keeps "you review and merge
  your board's PRs" as the stated default for a silent card, and says that a
  card naming a worker-side or branch-level owner overrides that default
  explicitly. No project or board name appears in the text, so it reads the same
  on every board; the default is unchanged.
- **A mis-rooted API server can no longer write — or delete — an operator
  profile and report success.** `hscc-api` reached profile files through three
  resolvers in one process (hermes `get_profile_dir`, the deliberately call-time
  ladder `routes_profile._hermes_profiles_dir`, and `rolelib.PROFILES_DIR`) and
  cross-checked none of them, while `hermes_constants._hermes_root_of` returns
  the NATIVE home for any `HERMES_HOME` that resolves *under* `~/.hermes`. Eight
  mutating sites were affected, not the two the hazard report named:
  `routes_profiles.py` create / **delete** / rename / describe-set, the profile
  editor's `config.yaml` + `profile.yaml` merge, `routes_bootstrap`'s
  `ensure_orchestrator` (which mints a whole `<proj>-orch` profile through
  `rolelib.PROFILES_DIR`), and the compaction-threshold ensure in
  `routes_orchestrator` — one per profile in the role sweep. The destructive one
  is delete: `delete_profile(name, yes=True)` removes a profile directory and the
  endpoint answered 200. Now `profile_root.py` gates it twice with one
  implementation: `assert_boot_intent()` runs before `resolve_config`,
  `load_token` and bind, so a mis-rooted server never serves at all and exits
  **2** on both entry paths (`python -m api_server serve` and the daemon's
  `hscc api start`) — a distinct code from the **1** a busy port or an unreadable
  token produces, so an operator can tell a misconfigured root from a transport
  problem — and `guard_write()` is the FIRST statement of every mutating backing,
  because the ladder re-points at call time by design and the boot assert alone
  would not keep "nothing written" true under that drift. A divergent write
  answers 503 `profile_root_mismatch` with the requested root, the
  `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`/`HERMES_REAL_HOME` triple and every divergent root named,
  in the same order the CLI refusal uses. Two deliberate non-503s: the
  compaction-threshold ensure is *incidental* to a chat or session-guard turn and
  documented fail-safe ("never break a chat"), so there the write is skipped and
  the divergence logged at ERROR while the request proceeds — turning a
  server-config state into a failed operator chat would be the worse bug — and the
  role-profile sweep checks once up front so a divergence costs one log line, not
  one per profile. Reads are left unguarded: a wrong-root read degrades to an
  honest empty list, it cannot corrupt a tree. Every boot now also prints
  `hscc-api: profiles root <realpath> (intent: none|<path>)`, which is what a
  wrong-root symptom gets diagnosed against.
- **A silently-ignored sandbox no longer reports success.** Setting
  `HERMES_HOME` was the only lever a harness had for a throwaway home, and it
  half-works: `hermes_constants._hermes_root_of` returns the NATIVE home for any
  `HERMES_HOME` that resolves *under* `~/.hermes`, so a throwaway home placed in
  a Hermes scratch dir — where Hermes scratch dirs live — resolves straight back
  to the live tree. Measured at `9422c740`, same probe, placement the only
  variable: `HERMES_HOME=<scratch under ~/.hermes/…>/.hermes` resolved
  `get_profile_dir("architect")` to the live `~/.hermes/profiles/architect`,
  while `HERMES_HOME=/tmp/<x>/.hermes` redirected correctly to
  `/tmp/<x>/.hermes/profiles/architect`. In the same first case
  `rolelib.PROFILES_DIR` *did* follow the throwaway — the two roots one run
  resolves can disagree, which is why a checker that reads only one of them saw
  a sandboxed run while the writer (per `changelog.d/t_10ccaf80.md`) wrote the
  operator's tree. Tests and CI now have a documented way to target another home
  and no longer have to relocate `HOME` to be safe.

## [2.15.10] - 2026-11-13

### Added
- **`hscc cards monitor` now streams what the worker thought, not only what it
  called.** Each per-card panel read only `content` plus one `┊` line per tool
  call, while a worker's thinking sits in the session store's reasoning
  columns. Measured on one operator session store (2026-11-13, read-only): of
  5424 assistant rows, 5396 carry reasoning and only 2116 carry any reply text
  at all — the majority of turns rendered as a bare tool line, which was the
  whole point of the panel. A panel now prints a row's reasoning above that
  row's reply text in dim italic, through the same `clean_line` + wrapping the
  rest of the body uses, collapsed to one line per row and cut at
  `REASON_PREVIEW` (320 chars) with an explicit `…+N more` marker — a measured
  thought reaches 70 KB, and one thought must not scroll the transcript off a
  panel that is a dozen rows tall. `t` stays the tools-only view it always
  was: a thinking line never passes `is_tool_line`. `reasoning` is read, and
  `reasoning_content` only as its fallback, never both — on that store the two
  columns hold identical text for every reasoning-bearing row, so a concat or
  a naive `COALESCE` would print every thought twice. Whether the columns
  exist is probed with `PRAGMA table_info` once per db file and cached, so a
  store that predates them reads the same rows and renders as before instead
  of landing in the blind-read error panel. The transcript page stays ONE
  definition — only the SELECT list varies, never the display set — and the
  read is the same additive, read-only `sqlite3` path with no `hermes_state`
  import, so the brew-installed CLI keeps working with no wrapper.

### Fixed
- **The sibling-gate premise was only as isolated as the caller's shell.** The
  failing pin builds a dep-less COPY venv and asserts `import rich` fails, so a
  sibling that can import the audit's deps cannot make the gate vacuous — but
  the scripts leg ran with a `PYTHONPATH` naming another interpreter's
  site-packages, and that handed `rich` to the venv (measured: the same
  assertion failed in two clean detached worktrees). Every child interpreter
  probe (`-sibling_is_runnable`, the (A)-only pass, its timeout calibration and
  the anti-vacuity capability check) now runs with `PYTHONPATH` /
  `PYTHONHOME` / `PYTHONUSERBASE` / `PYTHONSTARTUP` / `__PYVENV_LAUNCHER__`
  stripped from the child environment, and the import probes add `-I` so a
  candidate answers for itself. The premise assertion still demands a
  `ModuleNotFoundError` for `rich`: the pin got stricter, not weaker. The test
  now fabricates the exact leak (a hostile `PYTHONPATH` with a fake `rich`)
  and proves with a control child that the injection is real before the
  scrubbed probe rejects it, so a regression cannot pass as a green skip. No
  test in `scripts/tests/` mutates `os.environ["PYTHONPATH"]`; the injection
  came from the invoking environment, so the fix lives in the probe boundary.
## [2.15.9] - 2026-11-10

### Changed
- **Node addresses redacted repo-wide.** Real LAN node addresses committed in
  configs, docs, audits, the changelog and archived fixtures are replaced with
  the documented placeholder `10.0.0.x` (code defaults and fixtures use the
  RFC 5737 range `192.0.2.x`). Forward-only: no history rewrite and no tag
  amends, so older tags keep what they carried. `scripts/address_guard.py`
  now also rejects concrete `10.0.0.N` addresses.

### Fixed
- **The orchestrator waker's wake-once dedupe never suppressed anything.**
  `_claim_connect` handed out plain tuples while Hermes' claim helpers index
  rows by name, so every wake-claim read raised a `TypeError` that escaped the
  fail-open path; the waker treated every event as owed and logged "failing
  open towards delivering" per board per tick. It now sets `sqlite3.Row`, and
  tests drive Hermes' real claim helpers over the real connector (#290, #289).
- **Every dual-interpreter stamp was red before you touched anything.** Under

- **The cloud memory provider no longer shadows the installed `memori` SDK.**
  The repo staged it as `memori/` — a top-level package with the same import name
  as the third-party SDK the providers import (`from memori import Memori`).
  Any process with the repo root or `~/.hermes/plugins` on `sys.path` (e.g.
  `python -m pytest` from the repo root, `scripts/dep_pr_watcher.py`) resolved
  `memori` to the provider and the SDK became unimportable at all, because the
  SDK's own `__init__` performs absolute intra-package imports. Renamed the dir
  to `memori_cloud/`, matching the `memori_byodb/` sibling; the deployed plugin
  key and `plugin.yaml` name follow, and Hermes still loads it by file location.

  Existing hosts are migrated rather than left with both dirs:
  `install_payload.RETIRED_PAYLOAD = {"memori": "memori_cloud"}` moves a stale
  deployed `~/.hermes/plugins/memori/` to
  `plugins-backups/memori.retired.bak-<stamp>` on the next bootstrap, only when
  the replacement is installed in the same pass, and never deletes it.

  Guards: `scripts/verify_memori_sdk_shadowing.py` spawns a child per path root
  and FAILs (exit 1) unless `from memori import Memori, embed_texts` reaches the
  SDK; `scripts/tests/test_memori_sdk_shadowing.py` covers the mechanism with
  hermetic fixtures, pins that no top-level `memori/` returns, and loads the
  renamed provider the way Hermes does (`hermes_plugins.memori_cloud`).
  Measurement and the rejected options:
  `docs/audits/memori-sdk-shadowing-t_2ab0eda1.md`.
- **The memori embedding model is cached once per host, not once per cwd.**
  The memori SDK vendors the Rust `fastembed` crate inside
  `site-packages/memori_python.abi3.so`, and that crate's cache directory is the
  **relative** literal `.fastembed_cache` — the cwd of whichever process loaded
  the model. `strings` on the shipped `.so` shows both sides, the default and the
  override: `.fastembed_cachemodel_max_length=` and `FASTEMBED_CACHE_DIR`
  (alongside `HF_HOME` / `HF_ENDPOINT`), from `fastembed-5.13.1/src/common.rs`.
  Measured on the fleet host before this change: **nine** such roots, **88,984 KB
  each — 782.1 MB**, one model (`Qdrant/all-MiniLM-L6-v2-onnx`; the largest blob
  hashes identically, `bbd7b466…`, across all of them). They sat in five kanban
  worker workspaces on two boards, two `gateclerk` worktrees, `hermes-agent` (the
  gateway's `WorkingDirectory`), `~/.fastembed_cache`, and **the root of this
  repo** — that last one because `run_tests.sh` runs pytest with the repo root as
  cwd, so a suite could mint one as easily as an agent could.
  `t_ae3e5f9b`'s `.gitignore` rule (PR #279) only stops one being *committed*;
  this stops it being *written*.

  **The mechanism was proven, not assumed** — exporting a name the library
  ignores would pass an env-var check and change nothing, so
  `scripts/verify_fastembed_cache_dir.py` asserts where the bytes land. Three
  child processes, each with its own scratch cwd and its own `$HOME`, each making
  a real `memori.embed_texts` call (`dim=384`):

  | case | pinned? | landed in the pinned dir | cwd gained `.fastembed_cache` |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `red` | nothing | — (target never written) | **yes**, 16 files / 182,204,112 B |
  | `green` | `FASTEMBED_CACHE_DIR=<fresh, non-existent dir>` | **yes**, 16 files / 182,204,112 B | no |
  | `plugin` | unset in env; `import memori_byodb` set it | **yes** — under `$HOME/.cache/fastembed` | no |

  In `green` the named directory did not exist beforehand: the library created it,
  which is the knob being honoured by compiled Rust, not just echoed back by the
  environment. `red` is the non-vacuity half — the bug still reproduces, so the
  other two rows mean something. Each run prints the pre-existing root count before
  and after (`9 before, 9 after`) so a probe that leaked would report itself.

  **Where it is set: the provider, not a launcher.** The gateway's launchd plist
  does have an `EnvironmentVariables` dict (it is where every worker's
  `HSCC_MEMORI_AUGMENT_*` come from) but hermes' own installer
  (`hermes_cli/gateway_launchd_runtime.py`) writes and regenerates that file, and
  `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py:2884` gives each worker a scrubbed copy of the
  *dispatcher's* `os.environ` — so a plist edit would cover dispatched workers and
  nothing typed in a shell, no cron run, no TUI, no leg. Every one of those
  processes does import a memori provider, so `memori_byodb/__init__.py` pins it
  there, before anything in the package can reach the SDK, via
  `memori_byodb/_cache_env.py` (three rules: operator value wins; default
  `~/.cache/fastembed`, host-global and deliberately **not** under `$HERMES_HOME`,
  so profiles share one copy; **fail open** — an uncreatable or relative target
  leaves the environment untouched and logs a `WARN`, because a cache optimisation
  must never be able to break the memory provider). The cloud provider
  (`memori/`, also in `DEFAULT_PAYLOAD`) carries an identical copy — two plugins,
  no shared module path — and a leg test compares their ASTs so they cannot drift.
  `run_tests.sh` exports the same variable independently, so a leg cannot put 87 MB
  in the tree it is testing even if it never imports the provider.

  12 tests in `memori_byodb/tests/test_cache_env.py` (the whole `memori_byodb`
  leg collects 23; these 12 cover
  operator-wins precedence paired with a non-vacuity assertion that the two paths
  differ, fail-open on an uncreatable *and* on a relative target, the import-time
  wiring in a child process with a tmp `$HOME`, the call-site ordering as text, and
  the sibling-copy drift check) + 6 in
  `scripts/tests/test_run_tests_fastembed_cache.py`, which extracts the shipped
  runner block and executes it under bash. A new leg conftest for `memori_byodb`
  (the dir was already registered in `DIRS` but had no tests).

  Two findings surfaced by the probe, both recorded rather than quietly absorbed.
  (1) `hscc/memori/` — the cloud provider — **shadows the installed `memori` SDK**
  for any process whose `sys.path` contains it: measured as
  `ImportError: cannot import name 'embed_texts' from 'memori' (.../hscc/memori/__init__.py)`.
  Hermes does not hit it (it loads plugins by file location), so the probe and the
  leg test both use a one-symlink shim dir instead of putting the repo root on the
  path, and the conftest documents why the repo root stays off `sys.path`. Filed as

  and ~780 MB is the operator's call to reclaim (and `hscc` / `hermes-agent` may
  still be live). Once this deploys nothing writes to any of them; the command is
  in the decision record. Three probe trees from the verification runs remain under
  `$TMPDIR/fastembed-verify-*` (~260 MB) — their deletion is also left to the
  operator, as recursive delete is gated in a headless session.

  Decision record: `docs/audits/fastembed-cache-dir-t_317a0f30.md`.

  **Suite runs on this host** (py 3.14.9, `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv`, legs

## [2.15.8] - 2026-11-10

### Fixed
- **The orch-waker and the gateway notifier now wake an orchestrator ONCE per
  event, against a durable record instead of a cursor.** Both emitters read the
  same `task_events` row and each woke the orchestrator's REPL; the only thing
  they shared was `kanban_notify_subs.last_event_id`, which means "the notifier
  CONSUMED this event", not "the orchestrator was woken" — a `notify` sub, a
  sub seeded caught-up at boot, and a wake that raised all advance it without
  anyone taking a turn. §3.1 (hermes-agent#152206) put the real answer in the
  board DB — `kanban_wake_claims`, keyed by event identity alone
  (`profile`, `task_id`, `event_id` = the `task_events.id` the waker already
  carries), a lease until confirmed — but no emitter used it. `hscc_daemon/
  orch_waker.py` is now a citizen of that table: it suppresses on the read
  (`wake_already_claimed`, still `mode=ro`) at delivery-decision time beside the
  cursor ledger, takes the claim through hermes' OWN `try_claim_wake` after
  every gate and immediately before `repl_inject`, `confirm_wake`s on an
  accepted keystroke and `release_wake`s on a refused one (WakeNotAccepted), so
  a dead pane never leaves a row pretending otherwise. The semantics are
  borrowed, not re-derived — one lease, one CAS, one fail-open verdict — and
  the helpers are reached through the repo's single hermes-import seam
  (`autodown._load_kanban_db_or_default`), so a Hermes that predates §3.1 (or
  has it half-installed) resolves to "no claim knowledge", which means deliver.
  The timing is the safety property, and each rule is pinned: a claim taken on a
  tick that then stays quiet (debounce, min-gap, armed dead-pane backoff,
  `inject=None`) would mute the other emitter for `lease_s` for a wake nobody
  sent — a dropped wake dressed as a dedupe — so the take sits strictly between
  the last gate and the keystroke. Only kinds in `GATEWAY_WAKE_KINDS` are ever
  asked about: `spawn_failed` is scannable but not claimable, and a row written
  for it would be honoured by the notifier for a wake it can never make.
  Everything unknown fails open towards DELIVERING, including `PermissionError`
  from `write_txn`'s delegated-child guard (not a `sqlite3.Error`, so the
  adapter's own except is deliberately broader than hermes' helper's). Claim
  writes open the board `mode=rw` — never the bare path, so a stale enumeration
  entry fails instead of minting a board — and nothing else in a board is
  written: no task, event, run or subscription, and the card-to-human ping path
  is untouched. 29 tests in `hscc_daemon/tests/test_orch_waker_wake_claim.py`
  (28 red against the pre-fix code, and the other emitter modelled as the TABLE — lease-
  honouring, holder-only, fail-open — not as a stub that agrees with whatever is
  asked, which is how the fake caught its own wrong-direction reading of
  "cannot claim"); 5/5 mutation probes caught against a green unmutated control,
  one of which found the `mode=rw` gap this entry's test now closes.
- **The sqlite ignore rules are on `main` and now have a changelog entry; the
  card that asked for them had gone stale, not wrong.** `*.sqlite` and
  `*.sqlite3` are in `.gitignore` and live, measured in a clean checkout of
  `main` at `fc7c1caf`: `git check-ignore -v` names the **rules**, not
  positions — `…:*.sqlite  db.sqlite`, `…:*.sqlite3  probe.sqlite3` and
  `…:*.sqlite  hscc_daemon/nested.sqlite` — and a planted repo-root `db.sqlite`
  is invisible to `git add -A`. No line number is quoted, deliberately:
  `grep -n sqlite .gitignore` answered 75-76 at `8df6a352` and 84-85 at
  `fc7c1caf`, moved only by blocks other cards appended above them, so a pinned
  number goes false while the rule `check-ignore` names has not moved. No
  repo-root `db.sqlite` is tracked (`git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD |
  grep -i sqlite` → only `hscc-api/tests_gateway/diag_sqlite.py`, a source
  file), so the deletion half of `071fdb4e` is moot.
  **Nothing was landed by this card except this file.** The card's ask was
  written against `main` at `06a12aaf`; PR #275 squash-merged at
  `2026-11-10T02:54:34Z` into `8df6a352` and its head already carried
  `071fdb4e` (authored 01:56 UTC, before that merge), so the squash took the
  `.gitignore` hunk. Re-landing it would have been an empty diff, and no other
  PR was merged or touched as a side effect.
- **Probe lesson, recorded because the wrong probe is what produced the stale
  card: in a squash-merged repo, ancestry cannot answer "did this change land".**
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor 071fdb4e main` is `false` *at* `8df6a352` — the
  squash rewrote the commit — while the content is present and effective, and it
  is `false` at `fc7c1caf` too. The question "is this change on `main`" is a
  **tree** question, and the tree answer is scoped to the rules and pinned to a
  sha: `git diff --stat 071fdb4e 8df6a352 -- .gitignore` is **empty** — the file
  was byte-identical there, and that is what answered the question. It is *not*
  empty at `0a4db383` or later (`git diff --stat 071fdb4e 0a4db383 -- .gitignore`
  is `.gitignore | 9 +++++++++`, #279's unrelated `.fastembed_cache/` block), and
  the divergence grew again when #283 added the sidecar rules. What survives all
  of that is the **deletion column**: `git diff --numstat 071fdb4e origin/main
  -- .gitignore` reads `18 0` at `fc7c1caf` — eighteen lines added by other
  cards, **zero** removed — and `git show origin/main:.gitignore | grep -cx
  '*.sqlite'` is `1`, so neither rule has been edited since `071fdb4e`. The
  durable claim is therefore "the tree matched at `8df6a352`, and everything
  since is additive", not "the file is byte-identical to `main`": an append by
  someone else falsifies the latter without moving this change one inch. (Worth
  recording because this entry's own first correction repeated the mistake: it
  asserted the diff contained no sqlite line, and #283 merged a block full of
  them minutes later. The deletion column and `check-ignore` naming the rule were
  both still true.) Any card that opens on an ancestry check plus a
  `git branch -a --contains` roster is asserting where the *commit* is, not
  whether the *change* is, and will go stale the moment the PR it waits on merges.
- **The changelog half was the only real gap.** `071fdb4e`'s own stat is
  `.gitignore | 2 ++` + `db.sqlite | 0` — no fragment — and PR #275's squash
  fragment `changelog.d/t_2cd692f0.md` describes the orch-waker tests, never the
  ignore rules (`grep -n -i gitignore` on it → no match). So the rules reached a
  release candidate with nothing in `[Unreleased]` saying the repo now refuses
  sqlite artifacts, against `changelog.d/README.md` ("one file per card") and
  against the precedent the sibling `.gitignore` chore PR #279 set
  (`.gitignore` + `changelog.d/t_ae3e5f9b.md`).
- **SQLite's WAL companions can no longer ride into a commit on `git add -A`.**
  PR #275's fix (`071fdb4e`) added `*.sqlite` / `*.sqlite3` and its own message
  said the class was closed. It was not: `*.sqlite` matches the base file only,
  while the connection a WAL-mode database opens writes `db.sqlite-wal` and
  `db.sqlite-shm` **beside** it (`db.sqlite-journal` in rollback mode), and
  `git add -A` sees those three as ordinary new files. Measured in a clean clone
  of `origin/main` at `0a4db383` with paths git had never seen:
  `git check-ignore -v` named `.gitignore:84:*.sqlite` for `db.sqlite` and said
  nothing for any of the six sidecars probed (three at the root, three under
  `nested/`), and `git add -A --dry-run .` listed `add 'db.sqlite-wal'`,
  `'db.sqlite-shm'`, `'db.sqlite-journal'` and the three nested ones — base file
  ignored, companions staged. `*.sqlite-wal`, `*.sqlite-shm` and
  `*.sqlite-journal` now sit immediately after `*.sqlite` / `*.sqlite3` as one
  commented block, so the five sqlite rules stay together instead of scattering.
  Not extended to directory patterns: a trailing-`/` rule reads as absent for a
  path that does not exist yet, which makes a present rule look missing under
  `check-ignore` (the pitfall `t_ae3e5f9b` recorded).
  One gap in the same class stays open on purpose and is filed as its own card:
  sqlite names sidecars `<db>-wal`, so a `*.sqlite3` database writes
  `probe.sqlite3-wal` / `-shm` / `-journal`, which none of these patterns match.
- **A worker's board pin can no longer decide which board `hscc kanban pause`
  blocks, releases, or inventories.** `kanban_pause` shells out to the sanctioned
  CLI the same way the wedge gate does — `_run_hermes` ran
  `subprocess.run(["hermes", "kanban", …], timeout=60)` on the **inherited**
  environment — and one of its two calls is a WRITE. Hermes resolves a worker's
  `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` ahead of an explicit `--board` whenever a worker/delegation
  fence marker is set (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:540-555` →
  `agent/delegation_context.py:76-93`), and `board_pin`'s scrub only covers *our
  own* connection (a fork carries the environment copy made before the restore),
  so from a worker or delegated-child shell — which is what an orchestrator agent
  typing `hscc kanban pause <other-board>` is — `list_cards` inventoried the
  **pinned** board while the report named the board being paused, and `_hold`
  `reclaim`ed and `block`ed same-id cards **there** (ids are per-board). `resume`
  does the mirror through the same inherited env: `unblock` *releases* a hold the
  caller never placed. Both halves of `board-pin-fork-t_8616f2a5.md` §4, closed.
  Detection and wording stay `board_pin`'s; only the action crosses the fork, and
  it splits by access mode exactly as `board_pin` splits by `mode`. READ:
  `read_child_env` hands the probe a copy of the environment with
  `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` removed (warned once per pin+board in `board_pin`'s own
  wording) and `_run_hermes` forwards it — the only route by which a scrub
  survives `subprocess.run`; a legacy `run(argv)` cannot be handed one, so the
  read is refused and warned rather than answered from the wrong board. WRITE:
  `write_refusal(board)` is consulted at the top of each board's loop in `pause`,
  `resume` and `enforce`, and a conflicting board is refused **before anything
  spawns** — no `list`, no `reclaim`/`block`/`unblock`, no orchestrator steer, no
  cron park — and never enters the paused-state file, so a refused resume still
  knows the board is paused and `enforce` cannot retry a hold that never
  happened. The report is per board: `pause alpha beta` from a shell pinned at
  `alpha` pauses `alpha` and says `beta` was refused. A bare `_hold` call raises
  `BoardPinConflict` instead, having no report to write into. The write's
  environment is **never** scrubbed — that is the one thing `board_pin` §2c rules
  out, and it is why the fix is a refusal rather than the read's scrub. `enforce`
  reports what it could not do under a reserved `_refused` key that
  `enforce_tick` pops before its arithmetic, and stamps the stream `ok: False`
  with the pin named — `doctor_check`'s existing "last enforce tick FAILED … the
  hold is NOT being enforced" row, not a new shape for the reader half. No pin,
  no fence, or a pin that already *is* the board asked for keeps every call
  byte-identical (`run(argv)`, no `env`, child inherits) and says nothing; a lib
  that cannot answer `kanban_db_path` falls through to the untouched path.
  Hermes' precedence is untouched. 12 tests in
  `hscc_daemon/tests/test_board_pin_pause.py` — every conflict case paired with a
  non-vacuity assertion (the pre-guard `list` answers for the pinned board and the
  pre-guard `block` argv mutates its same-id card), the observables being the
  environment the child was handed, whether anything spawned at all, and what the
  report and the stream say — plus 13/13 decision points caught by mutation
  probes against a green unmutated control. Decision record:
  `docs/audits/board-pin-pause-t_70c97264.md`.
- **The dispatcher-wedge board-state gate no longer lets a worker's board pin
  decide what the CLI probes report.** The gate asks one question before it will
  restart the gateway — can a human reading `kanban list` / `kanban show` right
  now explain every ready card's zero spawn? — and it answers part of it through
  the sanctioned CLI, in a subprocess: `_default_gate_cli_runner` ran
  `subprocess.run(argv)` on the **inherited** environment and `_gate_cli_json`
  parsed whatever came back as fact. A dispatched worker or delegated shell
  carries `HERMES_KANBAN_DB`, and hermes resolves that pin ahead of `--board`
  whenever a fence marker is set (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:540-555` →
  `agent/delegation_context.py:76-93`), so the child printed the PINNED board's
  ready list and hold events while the gate labelled them with the board it had
  asked about — `"board 'X': all N ready cards explainably held [t_y:
  respawn_guarded:active_pr]"` built from a board nobody asked about, with a card
  id that lives elsewhere (ids are per-board). A real wedge could be explained
  away and its restart suppressed. `hscc_daemon/board_pin.py` is powerless across
  `subprocess.run`: it scrubs `os.environ` for the duration of *our* connection,
  and a forked child carries the copy made before the restore — so the only thing
  that reaches the child is an environment passed explicitly.
  The gate now computes the child environment per board through `board_pin`'s own
  detection (no re-derived path): when the pin would outrank `--board`, the probe
  is handed a copy of the environment with `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` removed and the
  override is warned once per (pin, board) in `board_pin`'s wording, naming both
  values; when the injected runner is the legacy `runner(argv)` shape and so
  cannot be handed one, the probe is never run at all and the board is reported
  `board state unverifiable` — the gate's existing fail-closed verdict, so the
  restart proceeds rather than resting on an explanation from the wrong board.
  No pin, no fence, or a pin that already *is* the board asked for → nothing is
  handed over and nothing is said (`cli_fn(argv)`, child inherits, argv
  byte-identical); a probe with no `board=` is left to the pin; `os.environ` is
  never mutated, so the read half of the fence is not weakened in our own
  process. The argv builders are untouched — `--board default` reaching the child
  is `t_dad0da32`'s half, and the same fork hazard in `kanban_pause`'s read *and*
  its `reclaim`/`block` writes is carded as `t_70c97264`. 10 tests in
  `hscc_daemon/tests/test_board_pin_gate_cli.py` — every conflict case paired with
  a non-vacuity assertion (the pre-change call, same armed env, answers the pinned
  board), the acceptance observable being the environment the CLI was handed and,
  in one case, `subprocess.run`'s own kwargs through the real runner — plus 8/8
  decision points caught by mutation probes against a green unmutated control.
  Decision record: `docs/audits/board-pin-fork-t_8616f2a5.md`.
- **`autodown._load_kanban_db_or_default` no longer leaves the Hermes agent tree
  on `sys.path` for the life of the process — and no other module needs it to.**
  The function documented that it put the resolved runtime dir on `sys.path`
  "only for the duration of this one import" and then left it at `sys.path[0]`;
  `kanban_live._load_hermes_config` and `profile_roster._hermes_gate` carried
  their own copy of the same insert, and nothing took the entry back out. In a
  daemon that is inert (one real tree). It is not inert in a test process — the
  leak is what turned one planted fake `hermes_cli` into poison every later
  consumer re-imported, even after an evictor had cleaned `sys.modules`
  (`docs/audits/orch-waker-import-leak_t_2be3b04e.md` §6, the production half PR
  #270 left open) — and it is not inert in the venv `/opt/homebrew/bin/hscc`
  runs in, where `dispatcher_wedge`'s five bare `from hermes_cli import …`
  readers could only answer because some *earlier* check had leaked the tree.
  One module owns the window now: `hscc_daemon/hermes_import.py`, with
  `agent_tree_on_path()` (and its one-line form `import_hermes()`) inserting the
  resolved dir and restoring `sys.path` in its `finally` — same entries, same
  order, exception path included. It is refcounted per path under a lock,
  because the daemon runs autodown and the wedge loop on their own threads and
  an unrefcounted restore would let the first window to finish pull the path out
  from under the other (a `ModuleNotFoundError` nobody could attribute). Every
  reader now opens its own window — autodown, kanban_live, dispatcher_wedge
  (five sites), escalate_watcher, profile_roster — so no answer depends on who
  ran first, which is the GAP-D-4 lesson applied to the wedge gate. Where a site
  *calls* into Hermes the call is inside the window too: a loaded package
  resolves its submodules through its own `__path__`, so the returned module
  needs no path, but a fresh top-level import triggered at call time does.
- **Deliberate test-expectation change (not collateral).**
  `test_kanban_live_caps.py::test_load_hermes_config_resolves_the_agent_tree_once`
  asserted `str(agent) in sys.path` *after* the call — it pinned the leak. It is
  now `…_then_closes_the_window` and asserts the opposite plus the non-vacuity
  half (the module it resolved has its `__file__` inside the planted tree and the
  gate serves nothing else, so the window undeniably opened). The pre-fix "second
  call must not duplicate" assertion is kept: the pre-fix code passed it, which is
  why the leak survived it. `autodown` gains the matching guard — the test quotes
  the promise out of the live docstring and plants a package that records
  `sys.path` at import time, so one test shows the tree held during the import
  and `sys.path` byte-identical afterwards.
- **`.fastembed_cache/` (87 MB of ONNX weights) can no longer ride into a commit
  on `git add -A`.** The directory was untracked and matched by no rule:
  `git check-ignore -v .fastembed_cache` exited 1 and `git status --short` listed
  `?? .fastembed_cache/`. This is the same class as the repo-root `db.sqlite`
  that a `git add -A` did commit in PR #275, and one `git add -A` from any worker
  would put 87 MB of model weights into the object store **permanently** — a
  `git rm` afterwards does not get the blobs back out.
  The rule is `.fastembed_cache/` in the *Runtime data — machine-specific state,
  never source* block rather than beside the sqlite rules the card pointed at,
  because runtime state is the truer home: this is not a source-tree artifact at
  all. The sqlite rules are not this entry's claim to make, and it makes none of
  its own: `*.sqlite` / `*.sqlite3` did reach `main` — `071fdb4e` landed with
  PR #275's squash `8df6a352` — and `changelog.d/t_2eb97ebb.md` (PR #281) is the
  fragment that records them, so nothing here re-states or re-measures them. The
  pattern `*.sqlite` does not match WAL sidecars (`db.sqlite-wal` / `-shm` /
  `-journal`) — those are t_4e553569's subject, not this entry's, and whether they
  are ignored now is its record to make, not this fragment's.
  **What writes it, so the rule is justified rather than swallowed:** no `.py` in
  this repo mentions fastembed (`grep -rn "fastembed" --include=*.py .` → 0 hits),
  because it is a *transitive* write. `memori_byodb/_client.py:90` does
  `from memori import Memori`, and the memori SDK (3.3.6) vendors the Rust
  `fastembed` crate — `memori_python.abi3.so` carries the literal
  `.fastembed_cache` default, the `FASTEMBED_CACHE_DIR` override, and the model
  table entry `AllMiniLML6V2 → Qdrant/all-MiniLM-L6-v2-onnx / model.onnx`, which
  is byte-for-byte the directory content
  (`models--Qdrant--all-MiniLM-L6-v2-onnx/{blobs,refs,snapshots}`). memori's
  default embedding model is exactly that one (`memori/_config.py:62`
  `self.model = "all-MiniLM-L6-v2"`). Because the cache path resolves under the
  **current working directory**, the download lands wherever an agent or test
  run happens to cwd — which is why this 87 MB copy at the repo root (Oct 28) is
  one of **seven** identical ones on this host, spread over `dev/hscc`, two
  `dev/gateclerk/.worktrees` roots and two `ecofire-bc` workspaces (Oct 8 → Nov 5):
  the cache follows cwd, not the project. A repo therefore cannot redirect it
  (that would need `FASTEMBED_CACHE_DIR` set by whoever spawns the agent — filed
  as follow-up work); it can only refuse to commit it. Hence ignore, not delete:
  the directory is a cache other runs reuse, and re-fetching costs bandwidth.
- **The "is this a planted fake `hermes_cli`?" rule has one definition again.**
  PR #270 (`t_2be3b04e`) stopped one test file's planted fake from deciding what
  a later file's board enumeration saw, and left the rule with **three** owners:
  conftest's `_is_planted_path` / `_hermes_cli_poison_reason`,
  `test_autodown.TestLoadKanbanDb._evict_planted_hermes_cli` (matched its own
  `tmp_path` *or* a substring of the pytest tmp-dir marker) and
  `test_board_pin._evict_planted_hermes_cli` (matched that marker alone). Three
  definitions of one hazard is how this class kept coming back — `t_b014c2b8`
  hit it from the other direction in `8e2283a7` — and the copies were already
  diverging: `test_board_pin`'s non-vacuity test built its stub under `/tmp`,
  which its own substring matched and conftest's temp-root rule did **not**, so
  the file was testing a rule nothing else in the suite agrees with.
  The predicate now lives in `hscc_daemon/tests/hermes_cli_plant.py` (moved
  verbatim: `is_planted_path`, `hermes_cli_names`, `poison_reason`,
  `purge_planted`, plus `evict_planted` which hands back what it removed so a
  borrower can restore it) and all four consumers import it. conftest keeps the
  autouse fixture and rebinds the shared objects under its historic private
  names, so `test_hermes_cli_import_isolation`'s `cf._…` probes are unchanged —
  and no test imports conftest to reach the rule, because a second import of
  conftest re-runs its module-level sparkrun-fence loader and swaps the live
  fence out from under the running suite. Each site keeps what is genuinely its
  own: `test_autodown` keeps the class-scoped finalizer (its own plant),
  `test_board_pin` keeps the borrow-and-`finally`-restore for `real_root`, and
  the nested probe file B keeps its own canary — now asked through the shared
  predicate instead of a re-derived `TEMP_ROOTS`.
  A fix that only moves text is not closed, so
  `hscc_daemon/tests/test_planted_hermes_cli_single_source.py` sweeps the
  package and fails if any tracked file re-`def`s a predicate function, carries
  the tmp-dir-marker or private-temp-root literal, or handles a plant without
  importing the owner; it also pins that conftest's `_…` names are *the same
  objects* as the module's, and that importing the module in a fresh interpreter
  changes neither `sys.path` nor the `hermes_cli`/fence cache. Guard proven
  non-vacuous by mutation probes (second `def` and marker literal each caught by
  the named check, unmutated control green). Behaviour is preserved where it was
  intentional; the one deliberate narrowing is that a path which merely contains
  the marker substring no longer counts as a plant — it was a false positive, and
  `hscc-cluster/tests/sparkrun_fence.py::_under_pytest_tmp` needs its *stricter*
  two-marker rule for a different question, so it stays out of scope (recorded in
  the guard's docstring so the next reader does not "unify" it).
- **A `.sqlite3` database's WAL companions can no longer ride into a commit on
  `git add -A`.** `t_4e553569` (PR #283) closed the `*.sqlite` half of this class
  and named the rest as its own open gap: sqlite names a database's companions
  `<db>-wal` / `<db>-shm` / `<db>-journal`, so the suffix family has to be spelled
  out per database extension — `*.sqlite-wal` does not match the sidecar a
  `.sqlite3` database writes, any more than `*.sqlite` matched the `.sqlite` one.
  Measured in a clean clone of `origin/main` at `fc7c1caf` (i.e. *after* #283
  landed) with paths git had never seen: `git check-ignore -v` printed nothing for
  `probe.sqlite3-wal`, `probe.sqlite3-shm`, `probe.sqlite3-journal`,
  `weird.sqlite3-wal` or the two under `nested/` (rc=1), and
  `git add -A --dry-run .` listed all seven of them. The same command, in the same
  directories at the same moment, stayed silent for `probe.sqlite-wal` /
  `-shm` — the two `*.sqlite` sidecars #283 had just made invisible — so the gap
  was the suffix and not the directory. `*.sqlite3-wal`, `*.sqlite3-shm` and
  `*.sqlite3-journal` now sit immediately after `*.sqlite-journal`, inside the same
  commented block, which the block's comment explains: both suffix families have to
  be listed because the sidecar name is built from the db name. They are listed
  per family rather than widened to `*-wal` / `*-shm` / `*-journal`, which would
  also sweep any unrelated file whose name happens to end in those words. No
  directory patterns, for the trailing-`/` reason `t_ae3e5f9b` recorded.
- **The dispatcher-wedge gate no longer hides the `default` board from itself.**
  `dispatcher_wedge`'s layer-2 board-state gate rebuilt autodown's `multi` flag
  from the *slug* — `bool(board) and board != "default"`, in the per-profile read
  and in both sanctioned-CLI argv builders — and `multi` is documented to mean
  exactly one thing to `board_pin.open_board`: *did the caller name a board?*
  (`board_pin.py:231-242`). So for `default` the gate said "no intent", the guard
  deferred to the worker's `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` pin, and the gate read **whatever
  board the pin pointed at while the panel reported `default`**. Not cosmetic: a
  card explained by a per-profile cap needs no further evidence, so the gate
  suppressed a gateway restart using `running` counts taken from a board it never
  read. Measured in a live worker shell: `list_boards()` returns 23 slugs
  *including `default`*, and `kanban_db_path(board="default")` is
  `<root>/kanban.db` with the pin scrubbed vs `<root>/kanban/boards/<slug>/kanban.db`
  with it visible — a different board's file.
  Split across three cards that reached the same hazard mid-flight: **t_147201fa
  (PR #271) removed the heuristic from the per-profile DB read**
  (`multi = hasattr(kanban_db, "list_boards")`) and **t_8616f2a5 (PR #274) stopped
  the CLI child inheriting the pin at all**. This card covers what both left —
  the two argv builders still omitted `--board default`, so `hermes kanban list`
  read whichever board `HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD` / the pin named while the answer was
  presented as `default` (a scrubbed child does not fix that: with the pin gone, an
  unnamed board still follows `HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD`), and `multi` was still re-derived
  per site instead of once per pass. Now `_gate_multi` holds that one rule and the
  answer is computed once per gate pass and threaded into `_board_ready_facts`,
  `_capped_assignees` and `_card_hold_from_cli`; both argv sites share one builder,
  `_gate_board_argv`, so the CLI argv and the DB open can no longer disagree about
  which board was named.
  `--board <slug>` is stated for every slug when the lib enumerates boards — the
  sanctioned CLI accepts `--board default` (measured: exit 0, valid JSON), so this
  is not a new contract. The legacy no-`list_boards` shape is byte-for-byte
  unchanged: no `--board`, `connect_closing()` with no `board=`, guard never
  consulted, no warning — which is also why the card's suggested
  `multi = bool(board)` was not used (it hands `multi=True` to a lib that cannot
  honour a board argument).
  8 tests in `hscc_daemon/tests/test_dispatcher_wedge_default_board_pin.py`, driving
  the real gate end-to-end with `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` + a fence marker armed and
  asserting observables only (the `WARN` line naming pin + both boards, the argv a
  human would type, which rows the probe read), each conflict case paired with a
  non-vacuity assertion that the same armed environment reads the WRONG board
  unguarded. Control probes: against `1b5e9eb0`-era code 4 of 8 fail; against
  `origin/main` after #271, and again after #274, 2 fail and both are the argv leak.
  Decision record: `docs/audits/wedge-default-board-pin-t_dad0da32.md`.
