### Docs
- **Operator runbook for the built-in orchestrator waker**
  (`docs/ops/orch-waker.md`, plus an `ops/` section in the `docs/README.md`
  index — the index had no `ops/` section when this card started, so
  `docs/ops/hermes-media.md` was unindexed too; PR #141 indexed it under
  *Reference* mid-review and the merge deduped it into the new `ops/` section,
  which matches the index's own directory-based convention).
  Documents the **shipped** shape of W1–W3 rather than the plan: the eight
  wake-worthy event kinds and their nudge labels; the four rate numbers (30 s
  stream cadence with `max(cadence, poll_s)` effective scan, 90 s debounce on
  the oldest pending line, 300 s per-board gap, 6-line dedup cap + `+N more`);
  the three skip rules (paused board via `kanban_paused.json`, no
  `~/.hermes/profiles/<board>-orch` directory, and a block whose `run_id` is
  NULL — the orch is not woken for its own action); the `~/.hscc/orch_waker.json`
  posture (default ON, fail-open on a missing/garbage file, knob typo falls back
  rather than making the loop hot, hot reload every tick); the
  `hscc orch waker status|enable|disable` verbs with their never-fabricate-when-
  empty rule; the waker-state and audit-JSONL schemas field by field; and the
  doctor verdict table, including why "enabled + never ticked + no daemon" is a
  warning and not a fatal (doctor is bootstrap's Stage-1 gate, the daemon has
  not started yet there).
  **Retirement note** (the operator's explicit ask, first section on the page):
  the built-in replaces `~/bin/orch-waker`, the unsupervised detached stopgap
  loop (no launchd job or plist names it; a reboot loses it) — exact retire
  order, and the one gate the operator must actually check. It is **not**
  the tick stamp: `status` prints a fresh stream tick even when zero boards are
  tracked, so the retirement check is two `status` reads a minute apart showing
  **board watermarks that moved**. The page also carries the reproduction and
  fix options for the blocker that makes the built-in inert until
  `t_fa9a2faf` lands (its `DEFAULT_STATE_PATH` and the daemon's stream-state file
  are the same `~/.hscc/state/orch_waker.json`, so every tick's stamp wipes the
  scan's `{last,pending,sent}` and each board re-tail-starts forever — 6 ticks
  over a board with one `completed` event: 0 nudges, audit file never created).
  Until then the stopgap stays the thing that wakes orchestrators.
- **Root-cause audit for the 2026-10-30/31 LiteLLM proxy `:4000` stalls**
  (`docs/audits/2026-10-31-proxy-stalls.md`). Investigation only, no fixes.
  Three findings, each with timestamped-log or `file:line` evidence: (a) the
  stall is inside the gateway but **not** an event-loop freeze — a five-path
  external poller stays evenly interleaved across all 17,376 access lines
  (max gap 46 lines), and autodiscover never restarted the router (0
  `reconciled` lines in 1,586 sweeps); (b) the daemon repair cannot recover
  because `_proxy_needs_restart` withholds `--restart` on a *timed-out* probe
  (so sparkrun answers `Proxy is already running (PID 91693)`), strict-consecutive
  streak math resets the escalation ladder on an intermittent healthy tick
  (17× "attempt 1 of 3", 0× "attempt 3"), and repair verification demands
  `port owner == tracked pid`, which a `uvx` wrapper launch can never satisfy
  (`grep -c "proxy repaired on" ~/.hscc/daemon.log` = **0**); (c) `FLEET
  VISIBILITY LOST` is a **symptom, not an independent fault** — neither sparkrun
  status path touches `:4000` (both SSH-sweep the nodes), so it must not be
  escalated as a second failure. Eight atomic fix proposals (FIX-1..FIX-8) with
  repo + `file:line` + acceptance + risk; sparkrun-side items are upstream
  proposals only.
- **`docs/ops/hermes-media.md` is now indexed in `docs/README.md`.** The M6
  ops recipe (t_ec488ce3, PR #130) shipped without an index line because its
  card's file whitelist stopped at the doc itself; the full-enumeration
  convention in `docs/README.md` ("every tracked file under `docs/` is
  enumerated below — one line each") was therefore broken by one. One
  Reference-section line, same style as the M0 `docs/design/media-serving.md`
  entry, marked **live** and pointing out that it is the client-side companion
  to that design doc. Follow-up card for the gap, as t_ec488ce3 asked.
- **Proxy-stall audit: question (c) — sparkrun status-sweep starvation — answered**
  (`docs/audits/2026-10-31-proxy-stalls.md` §8). Verdict: the sweep failed because
  **SSH was SLOW, not unreachable** — refuted as node-unreachable by `check_dgx`'s
  own in-tick `ssh PRIMARY echo reachable` succeeding on 11/14 degraded ticks and
  HTTP `/health` staying `3/3 online` for all 35 `FLEET VISIBILITY LOST` lines;
  host starvation refuted as the primary cause but confirmed as an amplifier
  (`run_cmd`'s cap is not a ceiling: measured 2.5–2.8× overshoot with an orphaned
  grandchild holding the pipe; all daemon streams slipped). Also records that the
  card's "Gateway check is SSH-dependent" premise is false (`check_gateway` is
  launchctl + `ps` + one local HTTP GET), that the daemon's 25 s/10 s caps sit
  *inside* the sweep's own 2 × 15 s budget so blindness is reachable from node
  slowness alone, and that `check_dgx` runs from four callers (60 s thread +
  watchdog 30 s + trigger 15 s), multiplying sweeps during an episode. Upstream
  FIX-7 restated with the arithmetic; a last-known-good fleet-visibility signal is
  proposed hscc-side, readable from the snapshot sparkrun already writes.
  Investigation only — no code changed.
- **Proxy stall audit: question (a) answered.** Appended §6 to
  `docs/audits/2026-10-31-proxy-stalls.md`, naming the per-request component
  that can delay a `/v1/chat/completions` by 16–24 s while the serving loop
  keeps answering everything else: LiteLLM 1.82.6's retry state machine —
  `await asyncio.sleep(retry_after)` at `litellm/router.py:5664`/`:5729` via
  `_time_to_sleep_before_retry` → `_calculate_retry_after` — under
  `Timeout(None)` (no upstream response timeout), SDK-level `max_retries = 2`,
  and a 5 s per-deployment cooldown gate. `docs/audits/t_c95a2137_analyze_access.py` and
  `docs/audits/t_c95a2137_shape_split.py` (new) reproduce the per-connection analysis that
  backs it. Also states that `litellm.log`
  contains **zero** lines from LiteLLM's own loggers (uvicorn-only capture, no
  `--detailed_debug`), so the retry path was silent by construction; refutes the
  `sparkrun_balancer.py:151` lock as the primary mechanism (a contended
  `threading.Lock` on the loop thread would stall all paths at once — the shape
  §2(a) already refuted), with its map-cardinality ground left open pending
  FIX-4; and reclassifies the "no listener" shape as uvicorn's unbounded
  graceful drain (`timeout_graceful_shutdown = None`, `uvicorn/server.py:281-300`)
  over never-finishing streams plus uvx wrapper-PID indirection — a
  shutdown-config gap, not a request-path defect. Identifies the
  `tcp_states.txt` loopback holders as Hermes worker/orchestrator processes
  (live `lsof` + socket sampler) and closes the poller question as client-side
  Ollama-dialect probing, with `/props` + `/version` still unattributed.
  Magnitude and trigger of the named delay remain **UNPROVEN**; §6.5 gives the
  capture recipe (`--detailed_debug`, timestamped access log, `py-spy` on the
  server child pid, backend `Retry-After` check, in-flight socket counts).
- **Escalation forensics for the 2026-10-31 proxy stalls — why window A's
  three escalated repairs logged no kill/reap line and failed.** New section
  `Question (b) — escalation forensics` (b5-b10) appended to
  `docs/audits/2026-10-31-proxy-stalls.md`, answering the one question PR #137
  left open (2(b) b4 + 4 item 3). Verdict per escalation: **the kill path was
  reached all three times** (the escalation banner is followed by an
  unconditional `_proxy_kill_hollow_tracked` call at `health.py:1292`) and each
  time returned through one of its **two silent exits**, because both of its
  inputs — sparkrun's tracked PID (`_proxy_tracked_pid`, `:1076-1090`) and the
  lsof port owner (`_proxy_listener`, `:1058-1073`) — failed without logging,
  exactly as every other sparkrun shell-out failed in that window. Kill/reap
  WARNs exist only on days the sparkrun CLI was reachable (10-27: 2, 10-29: 13,
  10-30: **0** against 27 `structured sparkrun status unavailable` WARNs), so
  the path is not broken — it is **blind, and silent about it**. Escalation #2
  closes by contradiction: its own `proxy start` printed `already running (PID
  46269)` minutes after the kill said nothing, proving a live tracked PID and
  therefore a failed status read. Escalation #3 **succeeded** — wrapper 91693
  and its uvicorn child 91757 were born inside it (`ps.txt` start times
  `23:50:29Z` / `23:50:46Z`, auto-discover's first sweep `23:50:40Z`) and served
  the fleet for 14 h — yet the daemon logged `proxy repair on :4000 FAILED`. The
  probe-mode flip is the witness the repair ignored: `timed out` (SYN accepted —
  a listener present) versus `[Errno 61] Connection refused` (nothing
  accepting); the post-repair probes date :4000's bind to `23:52:05Z`-`23:54:16Z`,
  **96-227 s after the wrapper was spawned against a 20 s
  `PROXY_REPAIR_VERIFY_WAIT_S`**, so escalated verification is defeated twice
  over (bind latency, then the uvx owner-vs-tracked mismatch) and FIX-2 must fix
  both. Section b9 lists the four exact log lines the fix cards must add; b7
  also shows an escalated repair can consume 305 s of wall clock against a
  nominal ~240 s of shell-out budgets while the 300 s cooldown counts it as one
  attempt (FIX-6), and that `sparkrun proxy status --json` itself issues a
  10-second request to the stalled proxy, which is why the tracked-PID read is
  the shell-out most likely to fail exactly when the repair needs it.
  Investigation only: no code changed, nothing live touched.

### schema
- **The orchestrator standard work-rules list now names the `orch_message`
  nudge channel.** `_PROJECT_ORCH_OPS` — the "## How you manage work" list
  every `<project>-orch` SOUL carries — gained rule 11: `orch_message` is how
  orchestrators nudge each other ("look at t_xxx on <board>, it's done/needs
  you"), never by commenting on DONE cards, and work itself always goes on a
  CARD on the right board (`--board` explicit). Documents the tool shipped on
  the parent card; without it an orchestrator has no prompt telling it the
  channel exists, so nudges keep landing as comments on already-finished
  cards. Live SOULs are updated by `hscc.py orch-sync`, never by hand-editing
  a profile.
- **Media recipe staging (`hscc-cluster/recipes/media/`): five SGLang
  Diffusion units + the offline validation gate.** Staged sources (operator
  installs to `~/.sparkrun-local/recipes/media/` per the dir README; nothing
  copies automatically) for the §8-Q1-locked tier picks:
  `qwen-image-gen-sgld` (FP8 weights-path over the diffusers base),
  `flux-klein-gen-sgld` (NVFP4 speed backup), `qwen-image-edit-sgld`
  (lmsys modelopt-NVFP4, self-describing repo), `wan-t2v-sgld` (lmsys FP8
  primary transformer; `transformer_2` BF16 = the sanctioned forced
  exception), `ltx-video-sgld` (online FP8; NVFP4 has no path for LTX).
  Every unit: digest-pinned single image, `distribution_config` off (staging
  lists in each header are the operator's contract — worker downloaded
  nothing), fraction as `defaults:` knob only, LAN-range unique ports
  30000–30004 with `--strict-ports`, `readiness.inference: false`,
  `--output-path`/`--input-save-path` scratch under the already-mounted
  `/cache/huggingface` root. `tests/test_media_recipes.py` is the offline
  gate CI can run (hscc-cluster cannot `import sparkrun`): sparkrun's
  load-path key allow-list, the §5/§7/§8 invariants, and — against a cached
  copy of the v0.5.22 **diffusion** argparse surface — every rendered
  `--flag`, including the dynamic `--component-*` map/alias grammar.
  That last check paid for itself immediately: the drafts carried
  `--mem-fraction-static` (sparkrun's LLM-side map spelling) and the
  diffusion parser **SystemExits on unrecognized args**
  (`server_args.py:3609`), so the fraction is now a sparkrun-level claim in
  `defaults:` only, never a CLI flag; proven non-vacuous by a mutation probe
  (injected srt-only flag → the check names it). Authoritative gate remains
  operator-side `sparkrun recipe validate` on the installed copy.
- **Template schema: `kind: image|video` on `ModelIntent` + a draft 1-worker
  media template (preview only — nothing was applied).** Media M4 per
  `docs/design/media-serving.md` §4. `ModelIntent` gains `kind` (validated at
  parse like `max_num_seqs`/`gpu_memory_utilization` — an enum
  `chat|image|video`, default `chat`, anything else a `TemplateIntentError`
  naming the key), carried unchanged through `ResolvedUnit.kind` by every
  placement branch, and written into a `serving.json` unit record ONLY when
  non-chat (the `uniform_pool` omit-if-default convention), so every existing
  template round-trips and every existing `serving.json` stays byte-identical.
  Serve-cmd rendering is UNCHANGED (§4: `kind` never enters argv, so declaring
  or changing it produces zero phantom drift — pinned by tests);
  `_KNOWN_MODEL_KEYS` accepts the key so structural validate stops calling it
  a typo. Model-level key, no schema-version bump (the #106 `max_num_seqs`
  precedent). Draft template `templates/3node/flux2-media.yaml` declares the
  two M1-staged media units — `media/flux-klein-gen-sgld.yaml` (FLUX.2-klein
  NVFP4, image) + `media/ltx-video-sgld.yaml` (LTX-2.5 FP8, video) — as
  `kind: image` / `kind: video` families. Two honest deviations from the card's
  example text: (1) the card named `flux2-dev-nvfp4`/`ltx-2.5-nvfp4`, but M1
  shipped FLUX.2-**klein**-9b-nvfp4 and LTX is FP8-NEVER-NVFP4 per its own
  recipe header + the §8-Q1 ruling, so the template points at the recipes that
  actually exist; (2) the card's "1 node" co-location would sum 0.25 + 0.70 =
  0.95 > the §5 hard rule (fraction sum ≤ 0.8 on a node, and the video unit
  cannot shrink below its declared working-set tier), so the two media units
  take one worker each (3-node template) instead of sharing one Spark. The
  kind-vs-recipe coherence leg (flipping `kind` without changing the recipe)
  is §4's "validate/doctor legs — built later" and is NOT in this card.
  PREVIEW ONLY: unit tests + `validate_template(structural_only=True)`-class
  dry paths with fakes only; no apply, no sparkrun exec (suite fence), no live
  cluster state.
- **Orchestrator-to-orchestrator messaging is now one documented stack: a CLI
  verb, a policed tool, and one SOUL rule.** Injecting into a running Hermes
  REPL used to need a private script, and an orchestrator that wanted to tell a
  peer something short had no bounded channel. `hscc-cluster/README.md` now
  carries the whole story under "Orchestrator-to-orchestrator messaging":
  `hscc orch inject <profile> "<message>" [--mode auto|plain|queue|steer]
  [--pane PANE] [--dry-run] [--json]` — a thin wrapper whose `--mode` passes
  straight through, whose `--dry-run` renders `repl_inject.format_plan` and
  sends nothing, and whose receipt keys and raise-based refusals are listed —
  plus the `orch_message(to, message, ref_card=None)` tool contract: the five
  rules enforced in code (orch-only both ends with the sender taken from the
  running profile and never an argument; queue-only `mode="auto"`; the
  `[from <sender-orch>] ` / `re: t_xxxx ` signature; the per-pair hourly cap and
  the `[from `-reply loop guard; the JSONL audit at
  `~/.hscc/state/orch_messages.jsonl` that is also the limiter's only state,
  hence fail-closed), the machine-readable refusal vocabulary, and the rate-cap
  knob — `orch_message.max_per_hour` in `~/.hscc/cluster.json` winning over
  `HSCC_ORCH_MSG_MAX_PER_HOUR`, default **6**, a garbage value falling through
  rather than switching the channel off or making it unlimited. It closes with
  the policy line that belongs to the channel and is *generated*, not written
  here: rule 11 of the `## How you manage work` block in
  `hscc-roles/generator.py` (PR #126) tells every `<project>-orch` SOUL that
  `orch_message` is the nudge, never the work order. `repl_inject` owns pane
  discovery, the exactly-one-pane rule and the mode→verb table, and neither
  surface re-implements it or runs `tmux` itself. Honest gap stated in the doc
  rather than papered over: the unified CLI's `orch` group branch
  (`hscc_daemon/hscc.py`) is still pending in follow-up card `t_5da7fd56`, so
  the README names the entry point that dispatches today and says how to tell
  when that note goes stale.
- **Media proxy registration decided: sparkrun autodiscovery + one proposed
  fork patch; `hscc-cluster/media_registration.py` is the shared contract.**
  The card asked: autodiscovery vs an explicit `model_list` entry emitted by
  `hscc apply`. The code answer (evidence in the module docstring, file:line
  against the live fork): explicit emission is not just wrong but structurally
  impossible on the sanctioned surface — `ProxyConfig` reads no `model_list`
  region from proxy.yaml at all (`proxy/config.py:166-340`), so a hand-merged
  entry would be read by nobody, and `hscc_daemon/declaration_agreement.py`
  flags a proxy.yaml `model_list` region as drift. Media units therefore
  register exactly like LLM units: `--served-model-name "<concrete> <alias>"`
  -> SGLang's mode-tagged `/v1/models` (M0 §2) -> sparkrun autodiscovery. The
  one thing no hscc code can deliver is `model_info.mode`: `DiscoveredEndpoint`
  carries no task-type field (`proxy/discovery.py:46-76`), so the mode tag
  lands via the smallest sparkrun addition spelled out in this card's PR body
  (map advertised `task_type`/`supported_task_types` to
  `model_info.mode: image_generation|video_generation` in
  `build_litellm_config`) — filed for the operator's fork, NOT patched here.
- **The mode contract exists once.** `KIND_TO_MODE` (image->image_generation,
  video->video_generation), the M0 §3 task-type mapping (`*2I|i2i` / `*2V|
  i2v|t2v`), the `/v1/models` parser (`advertised_media_models`), and
  `media_model_list_entry` — sparkrun's emission shape plus the one `mode`
  key, pinned so the fork patch and the hscc-side expectation cannot drift.
  Fail-closed by construction: no decidable mode raises instead of emitting an
  entry LiteLLM would list under `chat`, and a `kind` that contradicts the
  advertised task types is refused as a template bug. M4 validates through it;
  M5/M6 filter models by the same enum set. Chat units produce ZERO entries —
  untouched templates stay byte-identical (§7).
- **Orchestrators can now nudge each other, and only each other.** New tool
  `orch_message(to, message, ref_card=None)` in the `hscc-cluster` plugin: an
  orchestrator profile hands a short note to another orchestrator profile's
  live REPL through `repl_inject`, with the sender auto-signed
  `[from <sender-orch>] ` (plus `re: t_xxxx ` when `ref_card` names a task).
  Enforcement is in code, not prose: the sender is the *running* profile's
  identity and both ends must be `*-orch` profiles (workers and `default` are
  refused, and `to == sender` is refused as a loop); delivery is QUEUE-ONLY —
  `mode="auto"` (`/queue` while the target is busy, a plain send when idle) is
  the only mode this tool asks for, `steer` is never chosen, so a nudge cannot
  cut off a running turn; the pane must resolve to exactly one target (missing
  **or** ambiguous pane is a refusal, inherited from `repl_inject`, which this
  plugin does not reimplement). Per-`(sender, to)` rate limit of **6 messages
  per hour by default** (`orch_message.max_per_hour` in `~/.hscc/cluster.json`,
  `HSCC_ORCH_MSG_MAX_PER_HOUR` env override, file winning over env) plus a
  reply loop guard: a message that arrived already signed `[from ` may not be
  answered with another `orch_message` inside the same turn. Every call — sent
  **and** refused — appends one JSONL line to `~/.hscc/state/orch_messages.jsonl`
  with `ts`, `from`, `to`, `ref_card`, `chars`, `delivered`, `verb`, `reason`,
  `pane` and the first 200 characters of the body; the full body is never
  stored. That log is also the rate limiter's only state, so it is fail-closed:
  an unwritable audit log refuses the send before a pane is touched (an
  uncountable nudge is exactly what the loop guard exists to stop).
- **Media client enablement (M6): `image_gen` → proxy recipe + fleet
  `video_gen` `openai_compat` plugin.** New ops recipe
  `docs/ops/hermes-media.md`: `image_gen.provider=openai` +
  `image_gen.openai.base_url=http://10.0.0.x:4000/v1` with the model id sent
  verbatim (ruled first tier: `Qwen-Image-2.1-FP8` gen,
  `lmsys/qwen-image-edit-2511-modelopt-nvfp4-sglang` edit, `Wan2.2-T2V-A14B`
  video — §8 Q1), plus how to revert. Hermes' `video_generate` had no
  OpenAI-compatible provider, so the fleet ships one as a Hermes **plugin**
  (`install/hscc-plugins/video_gen/openai_compat/`, the M0 plugin-first
  placement — no core-hermes edit): `POST /v1/videos` → poll → content
  download per §2, ruling §8 Q5 honoured (no deadline, no size/seconds caps;
  ~5 s poll pacing only), poll-404 fails fast as the process-local job it is.
  `install_payload.PAYLOAD_EXTRA_DESTS` (new): a payload entry may additionally
  deploy at plugins_dir destinations beyond its staging path — required because
  Hermes' scanner recurses only ONE category level below the plugins dir, so
  the plugin must ALSO land at `<plugins>/video_gen/openai_compat/` (key
  `video_gen/openai_compat`, what `plugins.enabled` must carry). Additive, so
  `verify.check_plugin_payload`'s same-name comparisons keep working.
- **Templates can cap per-unit vLLM concurrency: per-model `max_num_seqs`.**
  `ModelIntent` gains an optional integer `max_num_seqs: <int >= 1>`, carried
  end-to-end exactly the way `gpu_memory_utilization` is (absent = the
  recipe's own default wins; validated at parse time so `hscc template
  validate` rejects a bad value — non-int, bool, or < 1 — offline instead of
  mid-provision). A resolved unit's serve command emits
  `sparkrun run ... -o max_num_seqs=N` (sparkrun's repeatable `-o key=value`
  override — there is no dedicated flag; verified against the live
  `sparkrun run --help`). Drift comparison handles a changed value the same
  way it handles a changed `--gpu-mem`: apply reports
  "serve command drift NOT applied ... -o max_num_seqs: '8' -> '5'" and
  leaves the running unit untouched until `--force-recreate`. Follows the
  PR #106 precedent for a model-level key (no schema-version bump — v4
  already exists for the declaration blocks). The shipped
  `4node/flash-next-all` now caps BOTH models at 5, honouring the operator
  rule of at most 5 running requests per node against the recipe's default
  of 8.

### Test
- **The PR/CI interlock's WARN-ONCE guarantee is now pinned by behaviour.**
  #135 restored it and #135's own acceptance asked for the pin, but no test
  ever asserted the cadence: `TestHasActivePrCi` covered the fail-safe
  polarity and the diagnosis, and nothing counted WARN lines. It had already
  regressed once exactly there — the `_PRCI_UNREACHABLE` branch called
  `_note_prci_active()` **after** `_note_prci_unavailable()`, and
  `_note_prci_active()` clears `warned`, so every 30s daemon tick re-armed the
  WARN and `~/.hscc/daemon.log` filled with one identical
  `Autodown PR/CI interlock unevaluable:` line per cycle while the fleet sat
  idle. Once-only now holds *by construction*, which is precisely the state in
  which a future "tidy up" of those two `_note_*` calls reintroduces the
  spam unnoticed. Two pins in
  `hscc_daemon/tests/test_autodown.py::TestHasActivePrCi`:
  `test_unreachable_warns_exactly_once_across_repeated_calls` (4 unreachable
  cycles ⇒ exactly **1** WARN, no line at any other level, and the repeat is
  silent *without* degrading the diagnosis — still `ok=False` + the
  `_PRCI_UNREACHABLE` sentinel) and
  `test_unreachable_warn_rearms_after_a_clear_screen` (unreachable → clear →
  unreachable ⇒ exactly **2** WARNs, one per outage, none from the clear
  screen — pinning that `_note_prci_clear()` resetting `warned` is the intended
  re-arm, not a leak). Both assert against the name the emitter actually
  calls, `autodown.log`, not `caplog`: `daemon_ops._get_logger` pins its
  rotating logger with `propagate = False`, so a root-logger handler sees
  **0** records however many WARNs fire — measured, not assumed
  (`daemon_ops.log("…", "WARN")` under a root handler: 0 records, file line
  written). A `caplog`-count pin would have passed forever either way. Each
  pin is mutation-checked against the three ways the guarantee can break: the
  pre-#135 `_note_prci_active()` clobber fails both pins, deleting
  `_note_prci_clear()`'s `warned` reset fails the re-arm pin (1 WARN, not 2),
  and dropping the `if not _PRCI_LOAD["warned"]` guard fails the once-pin
  (4 WARNs, not 1). No production change was needed — all three mutants were
  caught by tests alone.
## [2.14.0] - 2026-10-29

### Added
- **Panic-to-reboot sysctls installed cluster-wide by bootstrap.** A node
  hard-froze on 2026-10-27 with the journal dead mid-sentence and no BMC to
  reach — recovery was a human at the power button. `hscc bootstrap` now
  installs `/etc/sysctl.d/90-hscc-autoreboot.conf` on every sparkrun cluster
  node over the existing ssh path (`sudo -n`, never a password prompt):
  `kernel.panic=10`, `panic_on_oops=1`, `softlockup_panic=1`,
  `hung_task_panic=1` with `hung_task_timeout_secs=600` pinned alongside it
  (the deliberate choice against the 120s distro default — an ordinary NFS
  failover must not reboot a serving node), and `hardlockup_panic=1` only on
  kernels that expose the knob. Writes are atomic + content-compared
  (operator-edited file => drift report, never clobbered), every value is
  READ BACK and a mismatch fails that node loudly, `--dry-run` touches
  nothing, and `{"node_recovery": {"autoreboot": false}}` in cluster.json
  opts out. Doctor coverage arrives in the sibling card;
  `install_autoreboot.py` exports the expected-set constants for it.
- **Post-reboot relaunch for cluster-up-owned units.** A watchdog- or
  panic-triggered reboot left the node up but serving nothing: the auto-relaunch
  path refuses registered units by design (`lifecycle.py` — registered units
  launch ONLY through `hscc cluster up`), so the operator had to run
  `hscc cluster up` by hand. New `hscc_daemon/post_boot.py` adds a
  persisted `expected_up` marker (`~/.hscc/expected-up.json`, written by
  `hscc cluster up` / autodown wake, cleared by `hscc cluster down` / autodown
  teardown) plus a per-node boot-id baseline read through sparkrun's own
  transport. The daemon now relaunches a registered unit after a host reboot
  ONLY when every pre-existing gate already said the fleet is meant to be up:
  no intentional-autodown window, autodown lock free, heal lease free, the
  node's boot id actually changed, and the unit's health probe is down. The
  launch goes through the cluster-up surface itself (`cmd_cluster_up(nodes=…)`
  — one filter kwarg, not a second start path), the observed boot is recorded
  as baseline *before* launching so a same-boot repeat can never re-fire, and
  any missing evidence (marker absent, boot sweep failed, node unseen) means no
  action. `HSCC_POST_BOOT_RELAUNCH=0` disables the whole pass.
- **`hscc doctor` now answers "would this node come back on its own?".** The two
  node-recovery install layers had no coverage after install: a node could lose
  its watchdog arming or drift a panic knob and nothing would ever say so. The
  new `node recovery (watchdog + panic-to-reboot)` check probes every cluster
  node read-only over the sparkrun ssh path and reports per node: the hardware
  watchdog (`RuntimeWatchdogUSec` vs the installed 30s target, the watchdog
  core's sysfs state, and `wdctl`) and every managed sysctl the
  `/etc/sysctl.d/90-hscc-autoreboot.conf` drop-in declares (`kernel.panic=10`,
  `panic_on_oops`, `softlockup_panic`, `hung_task_panic` with
  `hung_task_timeout_secs=600`, and `hardlockup_panic` only where that kernel
  exposes it). Each red line names node + key + actual-vs-expected. It reuses
  the installers' own surfaces — `probe_node`/`is_armed_state`/
  `RUNTIME_WATCHDOG_SEC` and `probe_command`/`MANAGED_KEYS`/`build_dropin` — so
  doctor and bootstrap can never disagree about what protected means, and it
  adds no constants of its own.
- **An environment fault never reads as protection.** An unreachable node, a
  probe that dies before printing `HSCC_RC`, a `sudo -n` refusal, or a
  `/proc/sys` that names no knob renders as a check ERROR on that node naming
  the reason — never `armed/ok`, never a silent skip. The same rule covers the
  opt-outs: `node_recovery: {watchdog|autoreboot: false}` renders as *opted out*
  (`--`), not green, because "nothing enforces this" and "this is enforced" must
  not share a rendering. The check is non-fatal, like the install stages: an
  unprotected node is loud, but it never blocks an install.
- **Token counts in both monitors.** `hscc cluster monitor` gains `In` / `Out`
  columns (cumulative prompt / generated tokens per vLLM engine since it
  started, from `vllm:prompt_tokens_total` / `vllm:generation_tokens_total`)
  at every width, summed in the per-model total row. `hscc kanban monitor`
  shows each running card's worker-session tokens (`in/out`, matched by worker
  profile + run claim time against the profile's `state.db`
  `source='kanban'` session) and a 24 h total over every profile's kanban
  sessions; `--json` carries `tok_in` / `tok_out` / `tokens_24h`. Read-only,
  databases opened `mode=ro` and closed every pass.
- **`hscc kanban monitor [--live]`.** The kanban twin of `hscc cluster monitor
  --live`: running cards on every board (worker, run time, heartbeat age —
  >4h runs and >10 min silent heartbeats are flagged), ready cards waiting
  for a slot, per-board counts by status plus cards done in the last 24h, and
  the last hour's outcomes (completed / blocked / gave_up / crashed / …). The
  header shows the global `kanban.max_in_progress` slots in use and says when
  a full cap is stranding other boards' ready cards. `--board <slug>`,
  `--interval <s>`, `--json` snapshot. Read-only; reuses the autodown board
  enumeration that `hscc kanban stale` uses.
- **Nodes can now self-recover from a hard hang.** A DGX Spark has no BMC, so
  when `.244` froze solid on 2026-10-27 (journal stops mid-sentence, no panic,
  no oops, no softlockup line) the only recovery was a human at the power
  button ~2h later. `hscc-cluster/node_recovery.py` arms the GB10's unused
  SBSA hardware watchdog through systemd —
  `/etc/systemd/system.conf.d/90-hscc-watchdog.conf` with
  `RuntimeWatchdogSec=30s` + `RebootWatchdogSec=2min`, then `daemon-reexec` —
  so PID1 pets `/dev/watchdog0` and a hang resets the SoC instead of wedging.
  Installed by bootstrap (`Install: node hardware watchdog`, non-fatal,
  `--skip-node-recovery`); transport is sparkrun's own remote execution, root
  via `sudo -n` only, never a password prompt. Idempotent (content-compares,
  atomic same-dir rename), and it will not steal a device: an already-held
  `/dev/watchdog0` or an operator-edited drop-in is refused/reported as drift.
  Opt out with `node_recovery: {watchdog: false}` in `~/.hscc/cluster.json`
  (default ON when absent; subkeys are read independently, so the sysctl
  sibling's `autoreboot` can never disarm this). Probe surface for the doctor
  check: `probe_node()` / `is_armed_state()`.

### Fixed
- **`hscc verify` multiplex false-failed on two leftover directories, and
  `gateway.json` contradicted it with a different count.** Both multiplex
  scanners enumerated "every directory under `~/.hermes/profiles`", but the
  gateway builds `served_profiles` from Hermes' own enumeration
  (`hermes_cli.profiles._iter_named_profile_dirs`), which is narrower — so the
  check demanded the gateway serve profiles Hermes refuses to recognise, a
  requirement that can never be met. `profiles/.deleted/` (Hermes' tombstone
  dir, holding one 8-byte marker per deleted profile) was reported as a profile
  id named `.deleted`, and `profiles/ecofire-bc/` — a stub carrying only
  `workspaces/` and none of the six identity markers — as an unserved profile.
  The two surfaces also disagreed *with each other*: the daemon's scanner
  skipped dot-dirs and `verify`'s did not, so `gateway.json` said
  "1 profile(s) not served" while `hscc verify` named two. Both now share one
  roster helper, `hscc_daemon/profile_roster.list_profiles_on_disk`, which
  mirrors Hermes' gate (identity marker + profile-id grammar + not tombstoned
  + not parked), using Hermes' own predicates when `hermes_constants` is
  importable and a conservative mirror when it is not — the daemon deploys
  under `~/.hermes/plugins`, where it need not be. Coverage is NOT weakened: a
  directory that carries an identity marker and is unserved still fails, and
  names the missing profile on both surfaces. Measured on this host: the naive
  scan's expected-minus-served was `['.deleted', 'ecofire-bc']`; the shared
  gate's is `[]` (46 real profiles, all served).
- **`watchdog.json` reported "Degraded — gateway not reachable" while the
  gateway job and vLLM were both healthy.** Same root cause, not a separate
  defect: `check_gateway()` forces `ok=False` on a multiplex failure, and the
  watchdog copies that into its own verdict (and into the 3-failures-in-10min
  pipeline breaker). With the false-fail gone the stream reports healthy —
  `gateway.json` shows `gateway_job: true`, `vllm_healthy: true`,
  `multiplex_ok: true`. No no-op vLLM auto-restart is triggered by this check
  (`auto_restart_count` moves only on a `not dgx_ok` path), so the counter's
  270 is historical and untouched here.
- **`hscc cluster monitor --live` rendered every backend `down` under a
  Homebrew/Framework Python — `Errno 65 No route to host` on every LAN probe.**
  macOS ties Privacy > Local Network to the *signing identity* of the
  executable, so an adhoc-signed interpreter (a brew keg's `Python.app`) is
  denied on every private-range connect no matter how often the Python entries
  are re-toggled, while Apple-signed `/usr/bin/curl` reaches the same URL.
  Every LAN GET in HSCC went through `urllib`, so the whole serving table went
  red while the fleet was healthy (host stats survived because they ride ssh).
  All three LAN surfaces — `hscc_daemon/cluster_live.py::_http_get` (backend
  `/metrics` + proxy `/v1/model/info`), `hscc-bootstrap/doctor.py::
  _http_get_default` and its `hscc-cluster/cluster_template.py` mirror
  (Bearer-auth `/models` probes) — now retry that one failure through
  `/usr/bin/curl` as an **argv list** (never a shell) when, and only when,
  `urllib` reports errno **65 specifically** on a **private** host: RFC1918,
  `100.64.0.0/10` (tailnet CGNAT), `169.254/16` + `fe80::/10` link-local,
  `fc00::/7`, or `.local`. Loopback never falls back; Linux `EHOSTUNREACH` is
  113 and means genuinely no route, so it propagates untouched — as do
  `HTTPError`, timeouts and any public host. Parity is kept so callers still
  tell a probe/auth error from an unreachable endpoint: curl's `--fail` exit 22
  is mapped back to `urllib.error.HTTPError` carrying the status curl reported,
  every other curl exit to `URLError`. The `api_key` NEVER reaches argv (`ps`
  shows every token): the Bearer header goes through a `mkstemp` 0600 file curl
  reads with `-H @path`, unlinked in a `finally`. The notice —
  `LAN via curl fallback (Local Network permission)` — surfaces exactly once per
  process (`_lan_curl_reset_notice()` refills a consume-once ticket; the
  per-tick monitor cannot repeat it), on **stderr** so doctor's checklist and
  the template's `--json` stdout stay unpolluted and a daemon logs it once,
  then goes quiet. When `/usr/bin/curl` is missing or unusable the original
  errno-65 error surfaces with a one-line hint appended. The block is mirrored
  verbatim across the three standalone plugins (hyphenated plugin dirs are not
  importable, so no cross-plugin import) and pinned byte-identical by
  `hscc-cluster/tests/test_lan_curl_fallback.py`.
- **`project new --apply` died under the brew keg venv and left an orphan
  stub profile.** The keg venv carries only PyYAML/rich/psutil/markdown-it-py/
  mdurl/pygments (Formula/hscc.rb), so `ensure_session -> _open_profile_session_db`
  hit `ModuleNotFoundError: httpx` mid-import-chain, the session step died, and
  the just-created `<name>-orch` stub profile stayed behind with no registry
  entry — exactly the half-registered state the module docstring promises
  never to leave. The session-db opener now DELEGATES every runtime touch to
  the hermes venv interpreter as bounded JSON-line ops (Hermes' own
  SessionDB APIs on Hermes' own packages — nothing vendored into the keg, so
  no second package set to drift); `HSCC_HERMES_PYTHON` overrides resolution,
  which otherwise probes `$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent/venv/bin`, `~/.hermes/...`
  and PATH with a sentinel-verified import check. A profile CREATED in a run
  whose session step fails is rolled back through `hermes profile delete -y`
  (Hermes' own verb; a pre-existing profile is never touched), the ensure
  itself is one atomic create+title op, the registry write is a reported step
  instead of a crash, and the rerun path is idempotent (recreate -> ensure
  once -> registered). The **board step had the same wall** (create_board ->
  init_db -> lazy hermes_state -> httpx crashed the whole command): it now
  runs as remote ops on the same transport, and any raw provider crash there
  is reported as a failed step instead of escaping as a traceback. The
  environment-vs-data distinction is preserved verbatim: an unresolvable
  runtime raises `HermesRuntimeUnavailable` naming the missing module, never
  "profile has no state.db".
- **`hscc kanban stale --json` printed the human table.** The `hscc kanban`
  dispatcher (`kanban_blocked.cmd_kanban`) strips `--json` before delegating
  `stale`/`monitor` to `kanban_cli` and never handed it back; it is now
  re-appended on delegation.
- **"Watchdog configured" no longer counts as "watchdog armed".** systemd can
  adopt `RuntimeWatchdogSec` and still never open the device — e.g. a driver
  that does not advertise `WDIOF_CARDRESET`, or a PID1 that refused the reexec.
  A check on the config value alone would report those nodes protected while a
  hard hang wedges them exactly as before. `node_recovery.py` now reads the
  watchdog core's own sysfs `state` (and `wdctl`) and refuses to call a node
  armed while it reads `inactive`, in both `--arm` and `--probe`.

## [2.13.1] - 2026-10-25

### Added
- **Daemon single-instance claim — a second `run_daemon_loop` can no longer
  run beside the supervised one.** The engine-wedge double-probe incident
  (t_e37a74c7) traced its root emitter to TWO full daemon loops serving for
  2+ days: an orphaned `hscc start` fork whose pid label launchd's
  `start-daemon` later overwrote (`write_stopped()` + `save_pid()` re-labels
  supervision; it reaps nothing), while the orphan kept ticking every stream.
  New `daemon_singleton.py` takes an O_EXCL claim (`~/.hscc/daemon.lock`,
  deliberately the autodown `_acquire_lock` convention: holder recorded as
  `pid=N start=<ps lstart>`, liveness-first staleness with one
  break-and-retry) at `run_daemon_loop` entry — the single point BOTH entry
  paths reach — so no caller can bypass it. The CLI paths claim even earlier:
  the `cmd_start` grandchild claims BEFORE `save_pid()`, and
  `cmd_start_daemon` claims BEFORE `write_stopped()`, so a refused contender
  can never clobber the live holder's pid file; `cmd_start`'s parent now
  reports the grandchild's real verdict (a refusal prints an error panel
  instead of a false "started"). PID reuse — the case autodown's
  minutes-long lock never had to answer — is detected by pinning the holder
  to its `ps -o lstart` start time: same pid but different start ⇒ recycled ⇒
  breakable. A live holder renews its claim on every heartbeat tick, so a
  daemon running for months is never mistaken for abandoned; release is
  ownership-gated, and a SIGKILL'd holder is adjudicated dead by the next
  claim. A contender finds a live twin, waits out its (bounded) shutdown,
  then refuses LOUDLY and exits 3 — deliberately nonzero so launchd
  KeepAlive keeps retrying and supervision self-heals the moment the twin
  releases. Fail-open (with a WARN) only when the lock cannot be adjudicated
  at all: a daemon that will not boot over an unreadable lock file is worse
  than the old status quo. `hscc status` gained the twin surface: a portable
  `ps` scan of the two loop entry-point argv shapes
  (`hscc start` / `hscc.py start-daemon`; `hscc api start` etc. never match)
  prints "TWIN LOOP DETECTED" with the holder identity and the safe-kill
  guidance (SIGKILL the orphan — a TERM'd twin deletes the holder's pid file
  via `write_stopped()`), report-only, silence-by-contract on failure.
- **PATH shadow WARN on `hscc update --check` and `hscc bootstrap`.** When a
  Homebrew keg runs and an *earlier* `$PATH` entry holds a different `hscc` —
  the measured case is a conda env's `~/miniconda3/envs/<env>/bin/hscc` whose
  code is the deployed-plugins copy — a plain `hscc` silently runs that other
  copy, so the keg's newer verbs "do not exist". `update_check.detect_path_shadow()`
  now walks `$PATH` in order (not `shutil.which` — the ORDER is the question),
  skips the running install's own realpath, and flags an earlier hit that
  resolves elsewhere AND differs by version or install family (conda-env /
  user-local / deployed-plugins / brew / …). `update --check` prints a
  multi-line WARN naming the shadowing path, its version (an unresolvable
  version still warns, as "unknown version"), that the shadow is what plain
  `hscc` runs, and the *derived* explicit keg path (`sys.argv[0]` first, then
  a `bin/hscc` beside a source-tree ancestor — never a hardcoded
  `/opt/homebrew`); `bootstrap` (and `--dry-run`) print the same WARN before
  the installer runs, beside the CLI-shim stage. The scan is warn-only by
  construction: no deletion, no PATH or shell-rc edit, no uninstall — the
  last WARN line says so out loud. Silent when the PATH is clean and on any
  non-brew install mode; the offline-quiet contract is unchanged (a failed
  check still prints its single stderr line); `--json` only GAINS a `shadow`
  key (null when clean, and absent on a failure payload). A probe that hangs
  is cut off at 2 s and reported unknown, and a scan that somehow explodes
  internally returns None — it can never fail the check that called it.

### Fixed
- **Engine-wedge check stopped false-alarming `WEDGED unit(s) detected` on
  idle-healthy units (19 ERRORs on 2026-10-24, self-contradictory verdicts
  1.6 s apart).** Two independent defects, both fixed:
  (1) **One probe result per tick, shared across caller processes.** The
  live log proved the second caller was not a CLI run but a *second full
  daemon loop in a second process* (an orphaned `hscc start` fork alongside
  launchd's supervised `start-daemon` — both writers held `daemon.log`
  open, and the 60 s cadence doubled to a ~31 s mean inter-arrival with
  pass pairs 0–8 s apart). Each loop probed every unit with its own streak
  memory, so every "tick" fired two streaming probes per engine seconds
  apart and one transient blip counted twice — enough on its own to cross
  the 2-tick wedge debounce. An in-process memo cannot cover two processes,
  so each probe result is now recorded under the state dir (a
  `.probe`-suffixed file, deliberately outside the `*.json` stream glob
  that `status`/`verify` read); a caller consumes a recorded result only
  when it is newer than its own last probe of that unit and inside a short
  TTL (`HSCC_ENGINE_WEDGE_PROBE_SHARE_TTL`, default 20 s — well below the
  60 s cadence, so genuine next ticks and every debounce test still probe
  fresh), and an O_EXCL per-unit claim makes a caller WAIT (bounded by
  `ENGINE_WEDGE_PROBE_WAIT_CAP`, always < the probe bound) for a sibling's
  in-flight result instead of double-probing. Stale claims (holder died)
  are stolen, so sharing can never silence the check; a CLI
  `hscc check engine_wedge` run (under `persist_disabled`) neither reads
  nor publishes shares — an explicit operator request always probes fresh;
  orphaned share/claim files for removed units are pruned with the rest.
  (2) **`closed_early` is no longer wedge credit.** Every false wedge
  returned in 2.2–4.0 s across all 3 units while a genuine stall burns the
  full >=10 s bound each: the 200-stream *ended on its own* (peer close /
  RST race / early EOF — swallowed by the reader's bare except) with zero
  tokens, and the old code judged that identically to a stalled engine.
  `_probe_unit_generation` now reports this shape as `closed_early`: an
  inconclusive probe that accrues no wedge credit unless it SUSTAINS
  (`HSCC_ENGINE_WEDGE_INCONCLUSIVE_THRESHOLD`, default 3 consecutive), and
  even then the ordinary debounce plus the `/metrics` busy corroboration
  still apply before any wedge is declared. A stream that holds the FULL
  bound with zero tokens remains the unchanged wedge signature.
  `verify`'s `chat_roundtrip` corroborates `closed_early` against the
  generation counter exactly as it already did for `wedged`. The twin-loop
  condition itself (daemon single-instance enforcement) is deliberately
  out of scope here — it is an ops/launcher fix, filed as follow-up.

### Verified
- `hscc_daemon/tests/test_daemon_singleton.py`: **50** new cases; RED first
  (the 49-test set run against the base tree: 11 failed + 38 collection
  errors, 0 passed — the 50th pin was added after the RED check and passes
  only on the fixed tree):
  acquire (free/idempotent/live-twin-blocked/dead-holder-broken/pid-reuse-
  broken with a re-bound `lstart`/unparseable-age-rule/live-holder-never-
  broken-however-old), renew+release (ownership-gated both ways, mtime
  refresh, absent-safe), the entry hold() (live-twin refusal names the holder
  pid, stop_event aborts the wait early, release-during-wait reacquires,
  fail-open on unpreparable dir AND on adjudication crash while STILL
  refusing a real twin), the argv matcher (both loop shapes match;
  `hscc status`, `hscc api start --tailscale`, `hscc cluster monitor --live`,

  (twin line present/absent, `twin=None` UNKNOWN prints nothing, stale-claim
  note, exploded report stays silent), and the wiring pins: loop entry exits
  3 on refused claim BEFORE any boot step, entry points claim BEFORE
  pid-file bookkeeping (order-pinned for both `cmd_start_daemon` and the
  fork-emulated grandchild), refusal never reaches `save_pid`/loop (faithful
  `os._exit` emulation raises), heartbeat body renews on tick and survives a
  raising renewal.
- conftest registers `daemon_singleton.DAEMON_LOCK` in `_module_attrs` (the
  no-live-~/.hscc-leak contract) and pins the scan/adjudication seams
  (`_SCAN_OVERRIDE=0`, constant `_PS_START_OVERRIDE`, empty
  `_FAKE_ALIVE_PIDS`) suite-wide so no test observes the operator's live
  process table, plus `cli._START_VERDICT_TIMEOUT=0` for fork-emulating
  tests.
- Ops (same card): the live orphan (pid 29307, `hscc start` fork, PPID 1,
  27 `sample` threads = full twin loop) was SIGKILL'd after read-only
  verification that `~/.hscc/daemon.pid` named the launchd job (58499,
  `launchctl list` confirmed); single `lsof` writer verified after; the
  supervised daemon was never touched.
- Live E2E smokes (sandbox HOME + `HSCC_SPARKRUN_BIN` fake, zero live-fleet
  reach): `hscc start-daemon` against a lock whose holder is the REAL
  launchd daemon pid adjudicated LIVE → exit code 3, refusal ERROR logged
  with holder pid + lstart, pid file never created, foreign lock left

  /tmp/…/hscc start-daemon`, sleeps) running → exactly one "TWIN LOOP
  DETECTED: 2 daemon-loop processes" line (and the sh-wrapper filter proved
  itself by first refusing to count an sh-shebang stand-in).
- `python3 scripts/address_guard.py --tracked` rc=0,
  `scripts/run_tests.sh` ALL GREEN (frozen tree).
- `hscc_daemon/tests/test_update_check_shadow.py`: **49** new cases, all on

  warn-present (conda/local/deployed shims), warn-absent (clean PATH, later

- conftest pins `update_check.SHADOW_SCAN_MODES = ()` suite-wide so no

- `hscc_daemon/tests/test_update_check.py`: the NO-AUTO-UPGRADE static guard's

- `python3 scripts/address_guard.py --tracked` rc=0,
  `python3 scripts/changelog_fragments.py check` rc=0,
  `scripts/run_tests.sh` ALL GREEN (canonical venv, frozen tree).
- `hscc_daemon/tests/test_engine_wedge_double_probe.py`: **12** new cases +
  **2** in `test_verify.py` (TestCheckChatRoundtrip), RED against the shipped
  code (10 failed pre-fix) and green after. Classification: a real in-process
  fake engine whose SSE stream closes cleanly with zero tokens inside the
  bound yields `closed_early` (not `wedged`), while a fake that HOLDS the

  Check-level: fabricated idle-healthy units (metrics 0/0, chat 200 with

  Probe-share: a sibling caller's recorded result inside the TTL is consumed

## [2.13.0] - 2026-10-24

### Added
- **`hscc update --check` — the version check that never touches the
  install.** New read-only verb: queries the GitHub releases API for the
  latest tag (5 s timeout; authenticated `gh` when present, plain
  anonymous HTTPS otherwise, so public CI works), compares it to the
  `VERSION` file through the same `_get_version()` `hscc --version` uses,
  and prints the exact upgrade command for the detected install mode —
  `brew upgrade hscc` under Homebrew, `git -C <repo> pull` +
  `hscc bootstrap --yes` (script fallback named too) in a dev checkout,
  both commands when the layout is unrecognisable. NO auto-upgrade
  anywhere: the only write is the 24 h cache at
  `~/.hscc/update-check.json`. Install-mode detection prefers the
  `.hscc-brew-libexec` marker the tap drops (path-shape fallback), then a
  `.git` checkout — brew first, because a brew tree has no `.git` and
  would otherwise be told to `git pull` in a directory that is not a
  repo.
- **Cached once-a-day notices, loud/quiet per surface.** `hscc status`
  reads the cache ONLY (never fetches, can never fail) and appends one
  INFO line when the cache says newer and is ≤ 24 h old. The daemon
  piggybacks the daily check on the existing `run_heartbeat_loop` body —
  no new `PERIODIC_INTERVALS` stream — logs one WARN
  (`HSCC vX.Y.Z available (installed vA.B.C); upgrade: <cmd>`), never
  ERRORs, never raises. A failed check does not poison the cache: the
  last good answer survives on disk and the next run retries. The
  explicit verb is the only loud surface — offline or rate-limited it
  prints one short stderr line and exits 1.
- **`scripts/bump_formula.py` — the release step that bumps the Homebrew tap
  formula, so a tag lands in `pom11/homebrew-hscc` with no hand edits.**
  `Formula/hscc.rb` pins three facts about a release (archive `url`, its
  `sha256`, and the version Homebrew infers from the url) and all three used to
  be edited by hand at release time — the step that gets forgotten, after which
  the tap keeps serving the previous release while `CHANGELOG.md` and GitHub's
  `latest` say otherwise, with no symptom but a user silently installing an old
  build. `python3 scripts/bump_formula.py --tag v2.13.0` computes all three from
  the archive itself: **there is no `--sha256` flag**, because that digest is
  Homebrew's only integrity check for the tarball and a value copied from a
  release body is a value that can be wrong. The tag's version is cross-checked
  against the `VERSION` file **inside** the tarball — load-bearing, not
  belt-and-braces: the tap's `test do` asserts `hscc #{version}` against the tag
  while `hscc --version` prints the file, so a tag cut without bumping `VERSION`
  installs cleanly and then fails `brew test hscc` on every machine, and this is
  the one place that has the bytes to catch it.
  Only the release-pinned lines move: the formula's `resource` blocks pin PyPI,
  not hscc, so the rewrite asserts every changed line sits before the first
  `resource "` and that the number of `sha256` lines did not change (a formula
  shape that would swallow a PyPI digest fails loudly instead). It never *adds* a
  `version` line — the tap has none and `brew audit --strict` treats a redundant
  one as noise. `ruby -c` and the tap's vendored `address_guard.py --tracked`
  both run before the commit and restore the formula byte-for-byte if either
  rejects it; the guard is imported/shelled out to, never reimplemented, so this
  script carries no address pattern of its own. Idempotent: a current version
  exits `0` "up to date" (after re-hashing, so a stale digest is still
  corrected). Exit codes match `address_guard.py` (`2` = could not run: malformed
  tag, unreachable tarball, no ruby, no guard — never a silent pass).
  `.github/workflows/bump-homebrew-tap.yml.disabled` is the optional
  `on: release: published` transport, checked in inert: enabling it needs a
  cross-repo write token the operator creates, and it also gates on a
  `TAP_BUMP_ENABLED` repo variable so it can never paint every release red before
  that exists. No secret was created and none is enabled here.
- **`hscc bootstrap` verb + `--dry-run` + brew-libexec-aware CLI-shim skip.**
  `hscc bootstrap [flags]` locates `bootstrap.sh` relative to the resolved
  source root — repo checkout, deployed `$HERMES_HOME/plugins` copy, or a brew
  libexec tree (`<prefix>/Cellar/hscc/<ver>/libexec/hscc/`, version-stable as
  the shipped tap installs it; a versioned `libexec/hscc-<ver>/` is honoured
  too) — and execs it with every remaining argv token passed through
  (`--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--skip-*`); `HSCC_BOOTSTRAP_SH` overrides the lookup
  outright. `bootstrap.sh --dry-run` prints every planned write (plugin
  payload, CLI shim, watchdog scripts, git hooks, skills, role profiles,
  per-project orchestrators, `~/.hscc` state + serving.json, patches, config
  wiring, SOUL, review feature, trigger rules, daemon) and performs none.
  When the installer runs from a brew libexec root (marker file
  `.hscc-brew-libexec` if a tap writes one, or the `*/Cellar/*` /
  `*/libexec/hscc-*` path shapes — the shipped formula drops no marker, so
  `*/Cellar/*` is what fires on a real keg), the CLI-shim stage is SKIPPED
  with the reason printed — brew already owns `hscc` on PATH, and a shim
  into the Hermes venv would shadow it with a second, brew-invisible entry
  point.
  Non-brew trees keep the previous behaviour byte-for-byte. `hscc_cli`'s own
  `hscc_daemon` lookup gained a brew-libexec leg (ancestor `libexec/hscc` and
  `libexec/hscc-*` dirs, newest first, checked before `~/.hermes/plugins`) so
  a brew-installed `hscc` is self-contained: its venv lives inside
  `libexec/`, where the old sibling/repo candidates never saw the payload.

### Changed
- **README install story is brew-first.** `brew tap pom11/hscc && brew
  install hscc` followed by `hscc bootstrap --yes` is now THE quick start;
  the `git clone` + `bootstrap.sh` flow is relabelled "Install from source
  (development)" and is where a contributor goes, not where a user goes. The
  division of labour is stated where a reader will hit it: `brew install`
  stays inside its own keg and writes nothing into `~/.hermes` or `~/.hscc`,
  and `hscc bootstrap` is the step that does (with the CLI-shim stage skipped
  on a keg, because brew owns `hscc` on PATH), including the fallback the
  formula's own caveats print for a keg that predates the `bootstrap` verb.
  New **Upgrade** table — `brew upgrade hscc` + re-bootstrap vs `git pull` +
  re-bootstrap — and a new **Check whether you are behind** section
  documenting `hscc update --check` from the merged implementation: the quiet
  up-to-date one-liner, the `installed:` / `latest:` / `upgrade:` block, the
  one-line stderr + exit 1 offline behaviour, the 24 h cache at
  `~/.hscc/update-check.json` that `hscc status` reads without ever fetching,
  and the daemon's once-a-day WARN line. Every quoted command and every
  quoted output line was copied from the merged tree / merged tap formula,
  not written from memory. Docs only — no code changed.

  release: `up to date` is treated as a claim about the PUBLIC tap, so it is only
  made after the checkout has been synced onto origin and found to carry no
  unpushed commit — an unpushed bump commit is *published* (`status: bumped`,
  `recovered_push: true`) instead of being reported as fine, and with `--no-push`
  the run refuses rather than green-lighting a release the tap does not serve; the
  recovery push runs `ruby -c` and the guard over the committed tree first, because
  that commit was written by someone else and has never been through them; a
  pin that exists only as an uncommitted hand edit is refused, not committed as
  the tool's own work; a checkout that has diverged is refused, never rebased
  into public history; unpushed commits touching files besides the formula stop a
  push, because publishing an operator's private tap work to a public repo is a
  disclosure decision, not a release step; and a `git`/`ruby`/guard step that
  hangs surfaces as `CannotRun` (rc=2) naming the hung step, not a traceback.

- **`hscc cluster up` hung "forever" on an already-serving unit and starved
  the rest of the fleet.** The 2026-10-22 cooldown repro: a unit that already
  answered `/v1/models` 200 kept its `sparkrun run --no-follow --ensure` call
  open for 19 min (then 8 min on retry) while the SERIAL plan loop waited, so
  the other two units never launched. Three fixes in `cmd_cluster_up`:
  (1) each launch is bounded by a dedicated LAUNCH-PHASE timeout —
  `HSCC_CLUSTER_UP_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT`, default **180s**, deliberately NOT the
  1200s model-load grace — and an expiry is reported as that unit failing
  with the captured output tail, not swallowed; (2) a unit whose every span
  node already answers `/v1/models` with a parseable NON-EMPTY catalogue is
  reported already-up and sparkrun is never invoked (fail-open probe: any
  error = launch anyway, `--ensure` makes that safe); (3) launches run
  CONCURRENTLY over the independent hosts (ThreadPoolExecutor) while the
  per-unit report stays plan-ordered, and the A2 guard keeps its single
  prefetched status fetch. Sparkrun-side attribution (fix 4, source-read
  only, no hscc workaround): the hang is sparkrun's OWN readiness wait — in
  v0.4.1 `--ensure` "still wait[s] for readiness" and `--no-follow` only
  stops the log stream; `wait_for_run` blocks until the startup probe sees a
  first non-empty inference TOKEN, which a model that loads far past the
  port-bind can take ~66 min to deliver while `/v1/models` already answers
  200 — the operator's own hand-run log shows exactly that shape
  (`Waiting for server readiness... startup observation exceeded its
  deadline ... total 3947.3s`). The local `ssh ... bash -s` observation is
  that wait's per-poll SSH probe, not a missing-EOF bug: every `bash -s`
  site in sparkrun provably closes its stdin (`input=` or `communicate`).
  `--no-ready-wait` is the sparkrun-side flag that skips the wait; hscc
  deliberately does NOT pass it (the hscc launch timeout bounds the whole
  call instead, which also covers a genuinely wedged ssh).
- **`hscc_daemon.serving.resolve_cluster_config()`'s fallback could exec the
  operator's live sparkrun CLI — and on this host it DID, three times per
  daemon suite run.** The call was
  `subprocess.run("timeout 2 sparkrun cluster list --json", shell=True, ...)`:
  a shell string cannot be argv-rewritten by `sparkrun_bin.exec_argv`, so the
  `HSCC_SPARKRUN_BIN` hermetic pin never covered it (the daemon conftest's own
  docstring recorded exactly this gap). Now a LIST argv built by
  `sparkrun_bin.argv` — the repo's single execution chokepoint — with
  `shell=True` dropped and `timeout=3` replacing the PATH-dependent
  `timeout 2` wrapper (macOS keeps `timeout` in Homebrew). Pinned by
  `hscc_daemon/tests/test_serving_fallback_no_live_cli.py` against a fake CLI
  on a PATH-less HOME.

### Security
- **sparkrun argv FENCE at the conftest level (stop-work order; live `:4000`
  proxy SIGTERM incident).** One shared harness,
  `hscc-cluster/tests/sparkrun_fence.py`, wired into the four suites that can
  reach the CLI (`hscc-cluster`, `hscc-commands`, `hscc_daemon`,
  `sparkrun-hermes`): it wraps every subprocess entrypoint, resolves each
  argv element against PATH, and BLOCKS + FAILS the test whose call resolves
  to the operator's real sparkrun CLI (bare `sparkrun`, an absolute CLI path
  outside a pytest per-test tmp dir, a CLI at any LATER argv element, or the
  CLI name embedded in a `shell=True` string). Recipe paths named
  `sparkrun.yaml` are pinned as NOT CLI tokens (false-positive guard), and the
  sanctioned escape hatches are a `tmp_path` fake or an explicit
  expect-block — the fence reports blocked-vs-unexpected in the terminal
  summary every run. First run of the fence caught **six** real leak sites
  that had been silently exec'ing the operator's CLI in CI-shaped runs:
  `_pin_topology`'s `monkeypatch.setattr` reading lazy `clusterlib.HEAD/NODES/
  NAS_HOST` (→ live `sparkrun cluster list --json` for EVERY cluster test),
  a live discovery-cache WRITE from `test_discovery`, real `sparkrun show`
  per shipped recipe in `test_template_intent` (now opt-in gated), and the
  three `resolve_cluster_config` fallback shells above. Conftests now pin
  canned discovery output instead; no normal test run touches the fleet.
